If the loader started before the removal of its key or of one of its tags, on the same app instance, the fill or refresh does not store its value. The request still gets the value. Removing another key or tag does not affect the fill or refresh.
- A refresh that fails is logged as a warning, and the stale value stays. The next stale read tries again.

**Another store.** Props and SSR renders live in an `IInertiaCacheStore`. Register your own singleton before or after `AddInertia()`:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IInertiaCacheStore, MyRedisInertiaCacheStore>();
```

The store gets and sets byte arrays by `InertiaCacheKey`, removes by key and by tag, and reads unknown formats as a miss. While a page renders, a store that throws is logged, at most once every 30 seconds, and counts as a miss. `IInertiaCache` lets the exception through.

For a store shared by every app instance, `Inertia.Net.Redis` registers one with `AddInertiaRedisCache(...)`. See [Redis cache](/docs/redis).

## Typed page props

A typed object is AOT-friendly. Inertia.Net walks the object through its `JsonTypeInfo`. It resolves members of type `InertiaProp`, and the rest is serialized normally.

```csharp
public sealed class UsersPage
{
    public required IReadOnlyList<UserDto> Users { get; init; }
    public required InertiaProp Stats { get; init; }        // resolved by Inertia.Net
}

app.MapGet("/users", (AppDb db) => Render("Users/Index", new UsersPage
{
    Users = db.Users.Select(u => new UserDto(u.Id, u.Name)).ToList(),
    Stats = Defer(ct => db.StatsAsync(ct)),
}));
```

Under Native AOT, register `UsersPage` and its value types in your `JsonSerializerContext`. Anonymous types work only when reflection-based serialization is enabled, so they do not work under AOT.

## Dot keys

A top-level key containing dots is unpacked. `["user.name"] = "Ann"` becomes `"user": { "name": "Ann" }`. Cached props under dot keys use the cache too.

## BigInteger safety

With `o.PreserveBigIntegers = true`, integers beyond ±(2^53 − 1) are written as `{"$bigint":"9007199254740993"}` and the page gets `"preserveBigIntegers": true`.

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.PreserveBigIntegers = true);
```

## Rescue

`.Rescue()` keeps a page alive when one prop fails:

```csharp
["recommendations"] = Defer(ct => recs.GetAsync(ct)).Rescue(),
```

If the loader throws, Inertia.Net logs the exception and leaves the prop out of `props`. The prop's path goes to `"rescuedProps": ["recommendations"]`. Without `.Rescue()`, the exception propagates normally. Cancellation of the request is never rescued.

---

# Shared data

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/shared-data

> Share props with every page, statically or per request, and control the shared prop key list.

Shared props are merged into every page. Use them for values that every page needs and that are cheap to compute. When a page prop has the same key as a shared prop, the page prop wins.

## Register shared values

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.Share("appName", "Demo");                                      // static value
    o.Share("auth", ctx => new AuthInfo(ctx.User.Identity?.Name));   // per request
});
```

Share values from anywhere with an `HttpContext`, such as middleware or a handler:

```csharp
app.Use((context, next) =>
{
    context.Inertia().Share("locale", CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture.Name);
    return next(context);
});
```

The value can be any prop, including another factory:

```csharp
o.Share("permissions", ctx => Once(() => LoadPermissions(ctx)));
o.Share("plans", Once(() => plans.All()));   // like Laravel's shareOnce
```

`plans` is resolved once, and the client keeps it across visits.

`context.Inertia().FlushShared()` clears configured and request shared props for the current request only. It does not change
application defaults or other requests. Validation errors remain available. Call `Share(...)` afterwards to add replacement
request shares. To omit shared data on error pages only, set `InertiaErrorPagesOptions.IncludeSharedProps = false`.

## The shared prop key list

The top-level shared keys are listed in the page object so the client can keep them across navigations:

```json
{
  "props": { "errors": {}, "appName": "Demo", "auth": { "name": "Ada" } },
  "sharedProps": ["errors", "appName", "auth"]
}
```

`errors` is always shared, so the list always contains at least `"errors"`. Turn the list off with:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.ExposeSharedPropKeys = false);
```

## When to use shared props

Use shared props for values that every page needs and that are cheap to compute:

- the signed-in user or tenant name
- the application name and locale
- feature flags
- a once-per-client value such as a plan catalogue

Keep large or page-specific data in page props. Shared props are considered on every page response, including partial reloads, so keep them cheap or wrap an expensive value in `Once`.

<Callout type="tip" title="Share once">
Wrapping a shared value in `Once` is the equivalent of Laravel's `shareOnce`. The client keeps the value across visits and sends `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props`. The loader does not run again until the value expires.
</Callout>

## TypeScript

The generated declarations infer shared props from the values passed to `o.Share(...)`. Factories and per-request shares are typed as `unknown`. Use `o.TypeScript.SharedProps<T>()` when you want an explicit shape. See [TypeScript types](/docs/typescript).

---

# Validation

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/validation-and-errors

> Redirect back with validation errors for Minimal APIs, MVC and FastEndpoints, and add Precognition.

Inertia forms post, expect a redirect, and read validation errors from `props.errors` on the next page. Inertia.Net performs the redirect and carries the errors across it.

- A field maps to its **first** message. With `o.WithAllErrors = true` a field maps to an array of all its messages. The client's `form.withAllErrors()` expects that array.
- Error keys use dotted indices, for example `items.0.email`. A name uses the JSON member alias when metadata exposes one. Other members use the applicable naming policy. Dictionary keys are preserved. Minimal API and MVC use the page serializer’s HTTP JSON options. FastEndpoints uses its binding serializer policy. Two cases may fall back to naming-policy conversion: custom resolvers that omit member metadata, and paths without a model schema. Align field names and serializer settings.
- **Error bags.** An error bag is a named group of errors. The client sends `X-Inertia-Error-Bag: createUser` when the form has `errorBag="createUser"`. Errors arrive as `errors: { createUser: { email: "..." } }`. Without the header, `errors` is the flat object `{ email: "..." }`. A bag stored under a name other than `default` is always nested by bag name.

```ts
router.post('/users', data, { errorBag: 'createUser' })
```

## Validation libraries

| Backend | Validation |
|---|---|
| Minimal API | .NET 10 source-generated DataAnnotations through `AddValidation()`. `ValidationProblem` results. For FluentValidation, call `IValidator<T>` yourself and return `WithErrors`. |
| MVC | MVC model validation and `ModelState` |
| FastEndpoints | FastEndpoints validators, including FluentValidation |

## Minimal API

`WithInertiaValidation()` applies to a route or route group. It requires `services.AddValidation()`. Without validation resolvers, `WithInertiaValidation()` throws `InvalidOperationException` when the endpoint is constructed. Routing may construct endpoints lazily, so the exception does not always appear during application startup.

```csharp
builder.Services.AddValidation();

app.MapPost("/users", (CreateUserInput input, AppDb db) =>
{
    db.Add(input);
    return Results.Redirect("/users");
}).WithInertiaValidation();

app.MapGroup("/admin").WithInertiaValidation()
   .MapPost("/roles", (RoleInput input) => Results.Redirect("/admin/roles"));
```

For an Inertia request that is not a GET, a validation failure becomes a redirect back with the errors. The redirect status is 303 for PUT/PATCH/DELETE/QUERY. Every other client still gets the normal `400` validation problem. Inertia.Net converts a handler result the same way when the handler returns `TypedResults.ValidationProblem(...)`, `Results.ValidationProblem(...)` or an `HttpValidationProblemDetails`.

On .NET 11, async validators (`AsyncValidationAttribute`, `IAsyncValidatableObject`) report through `WithInertiaValidation()` and `WithInertiaPrecognition()` like synchronous attributes. A body that cannot be bound, such as malformed JSON, is still a `400` on both .NET 10 and .NET 11. It is never a redirect back without errors, and never a Precognition success.

<Callout type="warning" title="Why not rely on AddValidation alone?">
The built-in .NET 10 validation filter is added automatically and always runs outermost. It writes the 400 itself before any filter you add can see the failure. `WithInertiaValidation()` disables the built-in filter on the endpoint and runs the same source-generated validation itself. Do not combine `WithInertiaValidation()` with your own `.DisableValidation()`.
</Callout>

To report errors yourself, without attribute validation:

```csharp
app.MapPost("/login", (LoginInput input, SignInService auth) =>
    auth.TryLogin(input)
        ? Results.Redirect("/")
        : Back().WithErrors(new Dictionary<string, string>
        {
            ["email"] = "These credentials do not match.",
        }));
```

`Back().WithErrors(IDictionary<string, string[]> errors, string bag = "default")` also takes arrays of messages. Minimal API `AddValidation()` does not run FluentValidation automatically. Call a registered `IValidator<T>` yourself and map its failures:

```csharp
app.MapPost("/users", async (CreateUserInput input, IValidator<CreateUserInput> validator) =>
{
    var result = await validator.ValidateAsync(input);
    if (!result.IsValid)
    {
        var errors = result.Errors.GroupBy(e => e.PropertyName)
            .ToDictionary(g => g.Key, g => g.Select(e => e.ErrorMessage).ToArray());
        return Back().WithErrors(errors);
    }
    return Results.Redirect("/users");
});
```

Import `FluentValidation` and register your validator. Use the client's JSON field names as the dictionary keys when they differ from the validator's property names.

## MVC

`AddInertiaMvc()` registers a global filter. When an Inertia non-GET request has an invalid `ModelState`, the filter redirects back with the errors before the action runs. The errors go in the bag named by `X-Inertia-Error-Bag`. The default bag is `default`. `[ApiController]` controllers work too. For Inertia requests, the same redirect replaces their automatic 400.

```csharp
[HttpPost("/users")]
public IActionResult Store([FromBody] CreateUserInput input)
{
    if (!ModelState.IsValid) return ValidationProblem(ModelState);   // non-Inertia clients only
    db.Add(input);
    return Redirect("/users");
}
```

Binding failures get the generic message `The value is invalid.`, because their exception messages can expose internals.

## FastEndpoints

`c.ConfigureInertia()` adds a global pre-processor. A validation failure of an Inertia non-GET request becomes a redirect back with the errors. Other requests keep FastEndpoints' 400 JSON. FluentValidation validators work as usual.

```csharp
public sealed class CreateUserValidator : Validator<CreateUserRequest>
{
    public CreateUserValidator() => RuleFor(x => x.Email).NotEmpty().EmailAddress();
}

app.UseFastEndpoints(c => c.ConfigureInertia(ep => ep.AllowAnonymous()));
```

`c.ConfigureInertia()` works together with an existing `c.Endpoints.Configurator`. The optional callback of `c.ConfigureInertia()` runs after Inertia setup. The Inertia pre-processor runs after an endpoint's own pre-processors. If one of those already answered, for example with a 403, its answer wins.

## Precognition (live validation)

[Precognition](/docs/precognition) validates a request without running the handler. Minimal APIs use `.WithInertiaPrecognition()` instead of `.WithInertiaValidation()`. FastEndpoints enables Precognition with `ConfigureInertia()`. MVC does not support Precognition.

## Error bags in the client

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
const form = useForm({ name: '', email: '' })

<form onSubmit={(event) => {
  event.preventDefault()
  form.post('/users', { errorBag: 'createUser' })
}}>
  <input value={form.data.email} onChange={(event) => form.setData('email', event.target.value)} />
  <p>{form.errors.email}</p>
</form>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useForm } from '@inertiajs/vue3'

const form = useForm({ name: '', email: '' })
</script>

<template>
  <form @submit.prevent="form.post('/users', { errorBag: 'createUser' })">
    <input v-model="form.email" />
    <p>{{ form.errors.email }}</p>
  </form>
</template>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { useForm } from '@inertiajs/svelte'

  const form = useForm({ name: '', email: '' })

  function submit(event: SubmitEvent) {
    event.preventDefault()
    form.post('/users', { errorBag: 'createUser' })
  }
</script>

<form onsubmit={submit}>
  <input bind:value={form.email} />
  <p>{form.errors.email}</p>
</form>
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## All errors for a field

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.WithAllErrors = true);
```

With the option on, `errors.email` is an array of every message instead of the first.

## State and redirects

Validation errors travel in the state store across the redirect. By default the state store is an encrypted cookie. It can be a session or MVC TempData instead. See [Flash data](/docs/flash-data) for the store choices and size limits.

---

# Flash data

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/flash-data

> Carry a one-time message, toast or typed value across a redirect.

Flash data is a message or value for the next page, such as “Contact saved.” Unlike shared props, it is not kept in browser history.

Inertia.Net carries flash data across the redirect and any further redirects. The next response that is not a redirect consumes it. Flash data appears as `page.flash`, and only when there is some.

```csharp
app.MapPost("/users", (CreateUserInput input, HttpContext context) =>
{
    context.Inertia().Flash("toast", new { type = "success", message = "Saved" });
    return Results.Redirect("/users");
});

// or on Back():
return Back().WithFlash("toast", "Saved");
```

```json
{
  "component": "Users/Index",
  "props": { "errors": {} },
  "flash": { "toast": { "type": "success", "message": "Saved" } }
}
```

On the client, read flash data from the page's `flash` or from the `onFlash` visit callback. The page's `flash` is `usePage().flash`, or `page.flash` in Svelte:

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
const { flash } = usePage()

{flash.toast && <Toast {...flash.toast} />}
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { usePage } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
import Toast from './Toast.vue'

const page = usePage()
</script>

<template>
  <Toast v-if="page.flash.toast" v-bind="page.flash.toast" />
</template>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { page } from '@inertiajs/svelte'
  import Toast from './Toast.svelte'
</script>

{#if page.flash.toast}
  <Toast {...page.flash.toast} />
{/if}
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="info" title="Typed flash data">
The TypeScript generator can type `page.flash`. `FlashData<T>()` takes the whole flash object. For the `toast` above, use `record Flash(Toast? Toast)` and call `o.TypeScript.FlashData<Flash>()`. See [TypeScript types](/docs/typescript#flash-data).
</Callout>

Inertia forms keep their input on the client after `Back().WithErrors(...)`. They do not need a `WithInput()` helper. For a full-page form submission, choose only safe fields to flash before redirecting:

```csharp
return Back().WithFlash("old", new InertiaProps { ["email"] = email });
```

On the next page, read `flash.old` from the page and use the email to refill the field. Never flash passwords, tokens or other secrets.

## Remove a flash value

In a handler, call `http.Inertia().ForgetFlashed("toast", "user.name")` before rendering or redirecting.
This removes values set in this request or restored from a previous one. An exact key such as `"user.name"` wins over
the nested path. If no flash values remain, the page has no `flash` field. The remaining values still expire normally.

## Where state is kept

Some state must survive a redirect: flash data, errors, `clearHistory` and `preserveFragment`. When a request sets any of these and ends in a redirect, Inertia.Net saves the state in an `IInertiaStateStore`. The same applies when the request ends in a `Location()` / fragment `409`. Inertia.Net loads the state at the start of the next request. If the next request redirects again, the state is carried on, so `Back()` to a URL that itself redirects still shows the flash. Otherwise the response of the next request consumes the state. The state is also kept when the response is the version-mismatch `409`.

### Encrypted cookie (default)

The default store is an encrypted cookie named `.Inertia.State`. The cookie is protected with ASP.NET Core Data Protection, and it is `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax`. The store works without sessions and under Native AOT. Tampered or undecryptable cookies are ignored and deleted. The store logs a warning when the cookie is larger than about 4 KB, because browsers drop larger cookies.

### Session store

```csharp
builder.Services.AddSession();
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.State.UseSession());

app.UseSession();       // before UseInertia
app.UseInertia();
```

Use the session store when flash data can be large or must not reach the browser, and you already run sessions.

### MVC TempData store

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertiaMvc(o => o.UseTempDataStateStore());
```

This store keeps the state in MVC TempData, so the state follows your TempData provider. The provider is the default cookie provider, or `AddSessionStateTempDataProvider()` with `AddSession()` and `app.UseSession()` before `app.UseInertia()`. The store works for Minimal API endpoints too, because it saves TempData itself. It is not compatible with Native AOT.

### Your own store

Implement `IInertiaStateStore` and register it before `AddInertia`:

```csharp
public interface IInertiaStateStore
{
    ValueTask<byte[]?> LoadAsync(HttpContext httpContext);
    ValueTask SaveAsync(HttpContext httpContext, byte[] state);
    ValueTask ClearAsync(HttpContext httpContext);
}
```

The methods move opaque bytes. The format belongs to Inertia.Net.

## Choosing a store

| Store | Use when |
|---|---|
| Encrypted cookie | Default. Stateless, AOT safe, about 4 KB limit. |
| Session | Flash data can be large or must not reach the browser, and sessions already exist. |
| TempData | The app standardizes on MVC TempData, or you want to switch providers without changing code. |
| Custom | You need a shared store across instances or a different transport. |

<Callout type="warning" title="Multiple instances">
In a multi-instance deployment, configure Data Protection with a shared key ring. Otherwise the cookie written by one instance cannot be read by another.
</Callout>

## History flags

`encryptHistory` is written only when set and is not carried across redirects. `clearHistory` and `preserveFragment` go through the state store. They apply to the next page rendered after the redirects, and are then consumed.

```csharp
app.MapPost("/logout", (HttpContext context) =>
{
    context.Inertia().ClearHistory();
    return Results.Redirect("/login");
});
```

See [Redirects and history](/docs/redirects-and-history).

---

# Redirects and history

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/redirects-and-history

> Redirects, Back, Location, history encryption, clearing and URL fragments.

Inertia requests follow redirects with XHR, which is not always what the browser would do. Inertia.Net adjusts redirect responses so the client behaves correctly.

## Redirect helpers

```csharp
return Results.Redirect("/users");                 // standard redirect
return Back();                                     // Referer, else "~/" (app root, PathBase included)
return Back("/users");                             // Referer, else "/users"
return Location("https://billing.example.com");    // leave the SPA
```

`Back()` follows a `Referer` only when the `Referer` is an http(s) URL with the request's own host and port. When the `Referer` is unavailable, `Back()` tries the opt-in [previous URL](#previous-url) before the fallback. This prevents an open redirect. The scheme is not compared, so `Back()` works behind a TLS-terminating proxy. On HTTPS, an `http` Referer is upgraded to `https`.

## Previous URL

If a form returns `Back()` but the browser does not send its previous address (`Referer`), enable this option. For example, it helps when your site uses `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.State.RememberPreviousUrl = true);
```

After a successful page visit, a later `Back()` can use that saved address. `Back()` and the middleware's empty-response redirect look for a target in this order:

1. The same-host `Referer`.
2. The remembered URL.
3. The fallback.

`context.Inertia().PreviousUrl` reads the remembered URL. It returns `null` when the option is disabled, or when the remembered URL is absent or invalid. The remembered URL is user-controlled input, validated as a relative path.

Only successful status-200 page GET renders are remembered, including initial HTML visits. Partial reloads, prefetches, Precognition, non-GET requests and error pages are excluded. The value is the relative `PathBase + Path + QueryString`, without scheme or host. It is stored in the plain `.Inertia.Previous` session cookie. The cookie is `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/` and essential, and `Secure` follows `o.State.CookieSecurePolicy`. The cookie is written only when the URL changes. Set `o.State.PreviousUrlCookieName` to change the cookie name. The name must differ from `o.State.CookieName`.

The `.Inertia.Previous` cookie is used with both cookie and session state stores. It is **per browser, not per tab**: the most recent page render wins across tabs. The `Referer` still takes precedence when available.

## What the middleware changes

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| 302 for PUT, PATCH, DELETE or QUERY | Changed to **303 See Other**, so the browser follows with a GET |
| Redirect to another origin, non-prefetch | `409` with `X-Inertia-Location`: the client makes a full visit instead of an XHR the browser would block |
| Redirect whose `Location` contains `#`, non-prefetch | `409` with `X-Inertia-Redirect`: the client performs a full visit that keeps the fragment |
| `Location(url)` | `409` + `X-Inertia-Location` for Inertia requests, a plain `302` otherwise |
| Empty `200` response | Redirect back (302, or 303 for PUT/PATCH/DELETE/QUERY), using the same previous-URL and app-root fallback as `Back()` |
| `Vary` | `Vary: X-Inertia` is added to every response through the middleware |

Turn off external redirect conversion with `o.ConvertExternalRedirects = false` if the app intentionally redirects to another origin.

## Pages without a handler

```csharp
app.MapInertia("/about", "About", props);
```

`MapInertia` maps GET and HEAD to `Render("About", props)`, like Laravel's `Route::inertia`.

In MVC, `return this.InertiaView(props);` renders the action's own component. The default component name is `{Controller}/{Action}`. `AddInertiaMvc(o => o.ComponentResolver = ctx => ...)` changes the rule.

## History encryption

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.EncryptHistory = true);   // every page

context.Inertia().EncryptHistory();                          // this response
context.Inertia().EncryptHistory(false);                     // opt out for this response
```

`encryptHistory` is written as `true` only when set and is not carried across redirects. The Inertia client encrypts its history state with the page's key.

## Clearing history

```csharp
app.MapPost("/logout", (HttpContext context) =>
{
    context.Inertia().ClearHistory();
    return Results.Redirect("/login");
});
```

`clearHistory` goes through the state store. It applies to the next page rendered after the redirect(s), and is then consumed. It is typically used before a redirect after logout.

## Preserving a fragment

```csharp
context.Inertia().PreserveFragment();
```

By default a redirect loses the URL fragment. `PreserveFragment()` keeps it across the next redirect. The client receives `preserveFragment: true` on the next page.

## Page URL

The page object's `url` is PathBase, Path and QueryString. If your app runs behind a proxy that rewrites paths, set `o.UrlResolver` to return the URL that the browser sees:

```csharp
o.UrlResolver = ctx => ctx.Request.GetEncodedUrl();
```

<Callout type="tip" title="History state is in the cookie">
Flash data, errors, `clearHistory` and `preserveFragment` share the state store. By default the state store is an encrypted cookie. See [Flash data](/docs/flash-data#where-state-is-kept).
</Callout>

---

# Error pages

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/error-pages

> Render routing failures and unhandled exceptions as Inertia pages, with shared props and the original status.

When someone visits a missing page or the server encounters an error, you can show a page from your app instead of a blank response. Add this setup in `Program.cs` for production:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia();
builder.Services.AddInertiaErrorPages(o =>
{
    o.Component = "Error";                         // default
    o.Components[404] = "Errors/NotFound";          // optional per-status component
    o.StatusCodes = [403, 404, 500, 503];           // default
    o.Props = (context, status, exception) => new InertiaProps
    {
        ["requestId"] = context.TraceIdentifier,
    };
});

var app = builder.Build();
app.UseInertiaErrorPages();                        // before UseInertia and the endpoints
app.UseInertia();
```

A second Inertia UI mounted under its own path registers its own components with `AddInertiaErrorPages(name, ...)`. See
[Multiple apps and libraries](/docs/mounts).

Create the named components in your client pages directory. Each component receives:

- `status`
- the values from the optional `Props` callback
- shared props registered globally or through `context.Inertia().Share(...)`

The `Props` callback receives the exception for exception responses and `null` for status-code pages. Avoid returning exception
messages or stack traces to the client.

Set `o.IncludeSharedProps = false` to omit configured/request shared props and shared head tags from these error pages.
The `errors` prop and explicit error-page props (including `status`) remain available.

For example, `ClientApp/pages/Error.tsx` (`Error.vue` for Vue, `Error.svelte` for Svelte):

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
export default function Error({ status }: { status: number }) {
  const title = status === 404 ? 'Page not found'
    : status === 403 ? 'Access denied'
    : status === 503 ? 'Service unavailable'
    : 'Something went wrong'

  return <main><h1>{status}: {title}</h1><a href="/">Return home</a></main>
}
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue'

const props = defineProps<{ status: number }>()
const title = computed(() =>
  props.status === 404 ? 'Page not found'
    : props.status === 403 ? 'Access denied'
    : props.status === 503 ? 'Service unavailable'
    : 'Something went wrong',
)
</script>

<template>
  <main><h1>{{ status }}: {{ title }}</h1><a href="/">Return home</a></main>
</template>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  let { status }: { status: number } = $props()
  const title = $derived(
    status === 404 ? 'Page not found'
      : status === 403 ? 'Access denied'
      : status === 503 ? 'Service unavailable'
      : 'Something went wrong',
  )
</script>

<main><h1>{status}: {title}</h1><a href="/">Return home</a></main>
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The handler answers requests with `X-Inertia` or an `Accept: text/html` navigation. It preserves the error status. An XHR receives a
JSON page with `X-Inertia: true`. The first visit receives the normal root template. Root views and SSR work as for any other
render. When SSR is enabled, an error component must also resolve in your SSR bundle.

Only configured error statuses with an empty response are replaced. These are left to their existing handlers:

- API clients
- existing response bodies
- redirects
- Inertia's `409` responses
- antiforgery's `419` responses

Exceptions use the status selected by ASP.NET Core's exception middleware, which is 500 by default. The default statuses are 403, 404,
500 and 503. Extend `StatusCodes` to handle other error statuses. A page explicitly returned with
`Render(...).WithStatusCode(404)` keeps its component and props.

In Development, error pages are disabled so the developer exception page and Inertia debug modal stay available. Set
`o.EnabledInDevelopment = true` to preview your error components. The Inertia client renders non-2xx Inertia responses by default.
Application `httpException` event handlers or `onHttpException` callbacks can cancel that rendering.

## Already using `UseExceptionHandler()`
 `AddInertiaErrorPages()` registers an `IExceptionHandler` in the existing chain. Register
API-specific handlers first if they should take priority. Use one exception middleware. Then install only the status-code part:

```csharp
app.UseExceptionHandler();
app.UseInertiaErrorPages(useExceptionHandler: false);
app.UseInertia();
```

ASP.NET Core 10 suppresses exception diagnostics by default when an `IExceptionHandler` handles the exception. The Inertia
handler follows that policy and emits only a Debug message naming the rendered component. To keep the built-in exception logs
and diagnostics, configure the exception middleware explicitly:

```csharp
builder.Services.Configure<Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder.ExceptionHandlerOptions>(o =>
    o.SuppressDiagnosticsCallback = _ => false);
```

`AddInertiaErrorPages()` also registers the built-in ProblemDetails service as the exception middleware’s fallback. The Inertia
exception handler declines requests that do not ask for an Inertia page or HTML, so API exceptions use the host’s ProblemDetails
fallback and content negotiation. Existing ProblemDetails configuration and earlier application handlers still apply. Empty
status-code responses remain unchanged. Loaded flash and validation state is consumed when an error page renders, as on any other page response.

## Validation, SSR and rate limits

Validation redirects keep their existing behavior. The exception pipeline can handle a required SSR failure. Configure the error page so that it can render without relying on the same failed renderer. Rate-limit responses with an existing body are preserved. Configure the rejection response explicitly, including the Precognition header for validation requests. See [Precognition](/docs/precognition#rate-limiting).

---

# Authentication and rate limiting

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/authentication

> Redirect Inertia visits to the login page, send rate-limited forms back with a flash message, and start from the --auth template.

Use `UseInertiaRedirects()` to redirect Inertia visits to the login page, and `InertiaRateLimiting.OnRejected()` to send rate-limited forms back with a flash message. The `dotnet new inertia --auth` template creates an app with both.

## Cookie sign-in

The cookie handler answers an Inertia visit with 401, because the client sends `X-Requested-With`. Call `UseInertiaRedirects()` so that Inertia visits are redirected to the login page like browser requests. The redirect is a 303 after a `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`. `fetch` calls and Precognition validation keep their 401. When access is denied, the 403 error page renders if `AddInertiaErrorPages()` handles 403. Otherwise the request is redirected to `AccessDeniedPath`.

```csharp
builder.Services.AddAuthentication(CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
    .AddCookie(o =>
    {
        o.LoginPath = "/login";
        o.UseInertiaRedirects();   // after assigning o.Events, if you do: it wraps the handlers set there
    });

app.UseInertiaErrorPages();   // before UseAuthentication(): a 403 renders the Error page
app.UseInertia();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();
app.UseRateLimiter();         // after UseInertia(): see below
app.UseInertiaAntiforgery();
```

See [Error pages](/docs/error-pages) for the 403 and 429 pages.

## Rate limiting

`InertiaRateLimiting.OnRejected()` answers a rejected request the way the client expects:

- An Inertia form submission is redirected back with a flash message (`flash.error` by default) and `Retry-After`.
- A Precognition request gets 429 with `Precognition: true`.
- Anything else gets 429. When `AddInertiaErrorPages()` handles 429, Inertia requests get the error page instead.

```csharp
builder.Services.AddRateLimiter(o =>
{
    o.AddPolicy("login", http =>
    {
        var client = http.Connection.RemoteIpAddress?.ToString() ?? "unknown";
        // The metadata check keeps the Precognition header from skipping the limit on an endpoint whose handler runs for it.
        return http.GetEndpoint()?.Metadata.GetMetadata<InertiaPrecognitionMetadata>() is not null && InertiaPrecognition.IsPrecognitive(http.Request)
            ? RateLimitPartition.GetSlidingWindowLimiter("validation:" + client,
                _ => new SlidingWindowRateLimiterOptions { PermitLimit = 30, Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1), SegmentsPerWindow = 6 })
            : RateLimitPartition.GetFixedWindowLimiter("login:" + client,
                _ => new FixedWindowRateLimiterOptions { PermitLimit = 5, Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1) });
    });
    o.OnRejected = InertiaRateLimiting.OnRejected("error", "Too many attempts. Try again later.");
});

app.MapPost("/login", ...).WithInertiaPrecognition().RequireRateLimiting("login");
```

<Callout type="warning" title="Call UseRateLimiter() after UseInertia()">
Call `UseRateLimiter()` after `UseInertia()`, so the flash message of a rejected submission is saved.
</Callout>

## Start from the template

`dotnet new inertia --auth` creates an app with both:

```sh
dotnet new install Inertia.Net.Templates::1.9.8
dotnet new inertia -n MyApp --auth                # add --framework vue or svelte for another client
```

- A `/login` page whose form checks fields with [Precognition](/docs/precognition). The demo sign-in is demo@example.com / password, accepted only in Development.
- A protected `/dashboard`, and logout.
- The signed-in user shared as `auth.user`.
- A sign-in rate limit that sends the form back with a flash message.
- Inertia visits to a protected page are redirected to the login page (`UseInertiaRedirects()`). Signing in returns to the page that asked for it (`ReturnUrl`, local paths only).

The cookie handler sends signed-out visitors to `/login?ReturnUrl=/the/page`, and the login form posts the value back. Replace the in-memory `UserStore` with ASP.NET Core Identity or your user database.

---

# Head tags

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/head-tags

> Set the page title, meta and link tags on the server, in the first HTML response and on every visit.

Set the page's `<title>`, meta and link tags on the server. The tags are in the first HTML response. No JavaScript is needed, so crawlers and link previews see them. The tags are also sent with every visit as the `head` prop.

```csharp
return Render("Posts/Show", post).WithHead(h => h
    .Title(post.Title)
    .Meta("description", post.Summary)
    .Property("og:image", post.ImageUrl)
    .Link("canonical", $"https://example.com/posts/{post.Slug}"));
```

## A title template and per-request tags

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.Head.TitleTemplate = "{0} - My App");   // optional

// per request, e.g. middleware
app.Use((http, next) => { http.Inertia().Head.Meta("robots", "noindex"); return next(http); });
```

## On the client

```ts
createInertiaApp({ serverHead: true })   // the client keeps the tags up to date on every visit
```

Put `@inertiaHead` (or `<inertia-head />` in Razor) before the template's own `<title>`. See [the root template](/docs/pages-and-responses#the-root-template).

## How tags are keyed

- Values are HTML-encoded.
- Each tag is keyed (`data-inertia`) by `title`, the meta name or property, or the link rel. A later call with the same key replaces the tag. `Remove(key)` removes a tag that was set earlier, for example by middleware.
- With SSR the server-rendered head is used, which the client builds from the same prop.
- `o.Head.PropName` renames the prop.

In tests, `HasHead("title", "Users - App")` asserts a tag. See [Testing](/docs/testing).

---

# Partial reloads

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/partial-reloads

> Reload only the props a page needs with only and except filters.

In a partial reload, the Inertia client reloads the current page and asks for a subset of its props. Deferred props, polling and infinite scroll work this way. You can also use a partial reload directly for dashboard refresh buttons and filters. To refresh props when something changes on the server, without polling, use [live props](/docs/live-props).

## From the client

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
import { router } from '@inertiajs/react'

router.reload({ only: ['users'] })
router.reload({ except: ['permissions'] })
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```ts
import { router } from '@inertiajs/vue3'

router.reload({ only: ['users'] })
router.reload({ except: ['permissions'] })
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```ts
import { router } from '@inertiajs/svelte'

router.reload({ only: ['users'] })
router.reload({ except: ['permissions'] })
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

`router.visit('/users', { only: ['users'] })` works for a new page too. The client sends these headers:

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X-Inertia-Partial-Component` | The component being rendered |
| `X-Inertia-Partial-Data` | The `only` list |
| `X-Inertia-Partial-Except` | The `except` list |

Filtering applies only when the partial component equals the component being rendered.

## Server behavior

```csharp
["users"] = Prop(ct => db.Users.ToListAsync(ct)),    // runs on the partial reload above
["roles"] = Prop(ct => db.Roles.ToListAsync(ct)),    // does not run
```

- Paths are dot paths and match on a `.` boundary. `only: ["user"]` includes `user.name`. `only: ["user.name"]` includes `user.name` and keeps `user` as a container.
- `except` takes priority over `only`. `Always(...)` ignores both.
- The children of a value produced by a loader are not filtered. Nested literal `InertiaProps` are filtered.
- Loaders of excluded props never run.
- Selecting an array descendant (`rows.1.extra`) reloads the complete array, including sibling fields and nested loaders. A descendant `except` excludes the entire array. `Always` still wins.
- Omitted or rescued direct array elements keep their positions as `null`.
- A missing or empty list header means “no filter”, which differs from an empty list.

<Callout type="warning" title="Always wins">
`Always(...)` is sent even when a partial reload does not ask for it. Use it for props the page cannot render without. Do not use it for expensive data.
</Callout>

## What the client keeps

A reloaded prop replaces the client's value by default. A prop resolved from a loader is sent in full. To combine values instead, use [merge props](/docs/merging-props).

## Deferred and once props

Deferred props are loaded through partial reloads. `X-Inertia-Partial-Data` asks for the deferred group, and the server records which deferred props it has sent.

Once props that the reload asks for always resolve. The client sends `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props` with the keys it already holds, so the server can skip them while keeping the `onceProps` metadata.

## Testing partial reloads

`Inertia.Net.Testing` replays the request with the right headers:

```csharp
var page = await (await client.InertiaGetAsync("/dashboard")).GetInertiaPageAsync();

var only = await page.ReloadOnlyAsync(client, "users");
var except = await page.ReloadExceptAsync(client, "permissions");
var deferred = await page.LoadDeferredPropsAsync(client, "sidebar");
```

`ReloadOnlyAsync` asserts that the requested prop is present. `ReloadExceptAsync` asserts that the excluded prop is missing.

---

# Deferred props

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/deferred-props

> Load slow page sections after the first render, in groups.

`Defer` leaves a prop out of the first response and lists it under `deferredProps`. The client requests each group with a partial reload as soon as the page is mounted. The page becomes interactive without waiting for the slow data. A deferred prop can also be [live](/docs/live-props). A live deferred prop is fetched again whenever its event is broadcast.

```csharp
return Render("Dashboard", new InertiaProps
{
    ["user"] = user,
    ["stats"] = Defer(ct => reports.StatsAsync(ct)),
    ["chart"] = Defer(ct => reports.ChartAsync(ct), group: "charts"),
    ["activity"] = Defer(ct => reports.ActivityAsync(ct), group: "charts"),
});
```

```json
{
  "props": { "errors": {}, "user": { "name": "Ada" } },
  "deferredProps": {
    "default": ["stats"],
    "charts": ["chart", "activity"]
  }
}
```

<Sequence
  caption="Figure: the page paints first, then each deferred group arrives in its own partial reload."
  actors={[{ name: 'Browser', sub: 'Inertia client' }, { name: 'ASP.NET Core', sub: 'Dashboard route' }]}
  messages={[
    { from: 0, to: 1, text: 'GET /dashboard', phase: 'First paint' },
    { from: 1, to: 0, text: 'user now; stats, chart and activity left out', reply: true, code: '"deferredProps": { "default": ["stats"], "charts": [...] }' },
    { from: 0, to: 0, text: 'Page is interactive with skeletons showing' },
    { from: 0, to: 1, text: 'Group "default" in one partial reload', code: 'X-Inertia-Partial-Data: stats', phase: 'Deferred groups' },
    { from: 0, to: 1, text: 'Group "charts" in parallel', code: 'X-Inertia-Partial-Data: chart,activity' },
    { from: 1, to: 0, text: 'stats arrive, skeleton replaced', reply: true },
    { from: 1, to: 0, text: 'chart and activity arrive', reply: true },
  ]}
/>

Props in the same group load in one request. Different groups load in parallel requests. Inertia.Net only produces `deferredProps` on non-partial renders.

## The client

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
import { Deferred } from '@inertiajs/react'

<Deferred data="stats" fallback={<Spinner />}>
  <Stats />
</Deferred>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Deferred } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
import Spinner from './Spinner.vue'
import Stats from './Stats.vue'
</script>

<template>
  <Deferred data="stats">
    <template #fallback>
      <Spinner />
    </template>
    <Stats />
  </Deferred>
</template>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Deferred } from '@inertiajs/svelte'
  import Spinner from './Spinner.svelte'
  import Stats from './Stats.svelte'
</script>

<Deferred data="stats">
  {#snippet fallback()}
    <Spinner />
  {/snippet}
  <Stats />
</Deferred>
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The fallback is a prop in React, a `#fallback` slot in Vue and a `fallback` snippet in Svelte.

## Combining with other props

A deferred prop can also be merged, once or rescued:

```csharp
["posts"] = Defer(ct => db.Posts.Page(1).ToListAsync(ct)).Merge(),
["plans"] = Defer(ct => plans.AllAsync(ct)).Once(),
["recommendations"] = Defer(ct => recs.GetAsync(ct)).Rescue(),
```

The metadata combines: `deferredProps` lists the group, `mergeProps` lists the path, and `onceProps` records the key.

## Deferred scroll props

A deferred `Scroll(...)` prop reports `"posts.data"`, the same as a resolved one. This deliberately fixes a quirk in inertia-laravel:

```csharp
["posts"] = Scroll(page, wrapper: "data").Defer(),
```

## Testing

```csharp
var page = await (await client.InertiaGetAsync("/dashboard")).GetInertiaPageAsync();

new AssertableInertia(page).HasDeferred("sidebar", "stats").Missing("stats");

var loaded = await page.LoadDeferredPropsAsync(client, "sidebar");
new AssertableInertia(loaded).Has("stats");
```

See [Testing](/docs/testing) for the full assertion API.

<Callout type="tip" title="Use deferred props for below-the-fold data">
Use deferred props for data the page can render without. If the page means nothing until the data arrives, a normal prop is simpler.
</Callout>

---

# Merging props

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/merging-props

> Append, prepend, deep merge and match items instead of replacing the client's value.

By default, a reloaded prop replaces the client's value. A merge prop tells the client to combine the new value with the value it already has. Pagination, chat messages and incremental lists work this way.

| C\# | Metadata | Client behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `Merge(v)` | `mergeProps: ["key"]` | Append to the existing array |
| `Prop(...).Prepend()` | `prependProps: ["key"]` | Prepend |
| `Merge(v).Append("path")` | `mergeProps: ["key.path"]` | Append at a nested path |
| `Prop(...).Prepend("path")` | `prependProps: ["key.path"]` | Prepend at a nested path |
| `DeepMerge(v)` | `deepMergeProps: ["key"]` | Deep merge objects and arrays |
| `.MatchOn("id")` | `matchPropsOn: ["key.id"]` | Replace items with the same `id` instead of duplicating them |
| `.Append("path", matchOn: "id")` | `matchPropsOn: ["key.path.id"]` | The match key is relative to the nested path |

```csharp
["posts"] = Merge(ct => db.Posts.Page(page).ToListAsync(ct)).MatchOn("id"),
```

```json
{
  "mergeProps": ["posts"],
  "matchPropsOn": ["posts.id"]
}
```

## Nested paths

```csharp
["chat"] = Merge(chat).Append("messages", matchOn: "id"),
["notifications"] = Prop(() => next).Prepend("items"),
["settings"] = DeepMerge(settings),
```

```json
{
  "mergeProps": ["chat.messages", "notifications.items"],
  "deepMergeProps": ["settings"],
  "matchPropsOn": ["chat.messages.id"]
}
```

The path before the wrapper stays on the client. Only the value below the path is merged.

## Resetting a merge

The client can ask for a fresh value instead of a merge by listing the path in `X-Inertia-Reset`:

```ts
router.reload({ only: ['posts'], reset: ['posts'] })
```

Merge metadata is skipped for paths in the reset list. On partial reloads, it is also skipped for paths the reload did not ask for.

## Match on a stable key

`.MatchOn("id")` replaces an item with the same key instead of appending a duplicate. Use a stable, unique key from your data. Without a match key, incremental updates append every item again.

```csharp
["messages"] = Merge(page.Items).MatchOn("id"),
```

## Deep merge

`DeepMerge` recursively combines objects. Arrays are merged by index. Use `MatchOn` when you need item identity.

```csharp
["filters"] = DeepMerge(new { search, tags }),
```

<Callout type="info" title="Merge metadata and partial reloads">
On a partial reload, merge metadata is only emitted for paths the reload asked for. `Always` still applies independently.
</Callout>

---

# Once props

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/once-props

> Remember expensive values on the client and skip them on later visits.

Use once props for expensive values that rarely change. The client remembers a once prop across visits. It tells the server which keys it holds with `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props`, so the server can skip them on later visits.

```csharp
["countries"] = Once(ct => db.CountriesAsync(ct)),                                  // key = the prop path
["plans"]     = Once(ct => db.PlansAsync(ct)).As("billing-plans"),                   // custom key
["rates"]     = Once(ct => fx.RatesAsync(ct)).Until(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10)),       // client expires it
["tax"]       = Once(ct => db.TaxAsync(ct)).Fresh(),                                 // always re-send
["flags"]     = Prop(ct => db.FlagsAsync(ct)).Once(key: "flags", until: TimeSpan.FromHours(1)),
```

```json
{
  "props": { "errors": {}, "countries": [ { "code": "US" } ] },
  "onceProps": {
    "countries": { "prop": "countries", "expiresAt": null },
    "billing-plans": { "prop": "plans", "expiresAt": 1760000000000 }
  }
}
```

## Behavior

- The value is left out on later visits, but the `onceProps` entry stays so the client keeps its copy.
- `.Fresh()` sends the value even when the client has it.
- Partial reloads always resolve once props that the reload asks for.
- Expiry is computed from the registered `TimeProvider`, so tests can use `FakeTimeProvider`.
- `.As(key)` and `.Until(ttl)` imply once.
- Sharing a key between pages lets the client reuse one value across them.

## Keys

The default key is the prop path. Use `.As("billing-plans")` when the same value is exposed under different names, or when you want a stable key across page changes.

```csharp
["plans"] = Once(ct => plans.AllAsync(ct)).As("billing-plans"),
```

<Callout type="warning" title="A key is a value identity">
Two props that share a key are treated as the same client value. Only share a key when the values are the same. If you are not sure, use the default prop path.
</Callout>

## Expiry

`.Until(TimeSpan)` sets `expiresAt` in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The client stops treating the key as loaded after that time and requests the value again. The server leaves the value out only when the client lists the key in `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props`.

## Shared once props

```csharp
o.Share("plans", Once(() => plans.All()));
```

A shared once prop is the equivalent of Laravel's `shareOnce`. The client keeps the value across visits.

## Testing

`InertiaPage.OnceProps` exposes the metadata:

```csharp
var page = await (await client.InertiaGetAsync("/billing")).GetInertiaPageAsync();
Assert.True(page.OnceProps.ContainsKey("billing-plans"));
```

Revisit the page with the same client and assert that the prop is missing while `onceProps` remains.

---

# Infinite scroll

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/infinite-scroll

> Merge pages of items and report paging metadata to the InfiniteScroll client component.

Use infinite scroll when a reader should see more items as they reach the end of a list. `Scroll(...)` merges the items inside a value and reports paging metadata to the `<InfiniteScroll>` client component. The items sit in the *wrapper*, which is `"data"` by default.

```csharp
app.MapGet("/feed", (PageRequest request) => Render("Feed", new InertiaProps
{
    ["posts"] = Scroll(Pagination.Paginate(AppState.Posts, request)),
}));
```

```json
{
  "props": { "errors": {}, "posts": { "data": [ { "id": 21 } ] } },
  "mergeProps": ["posts.data"],
  "scrollProps": {
    "posts": { "pageName": "page", "previousPage": 1, "nextPage": 3, "currentPage": 2, "reset": false }
  }
}
```

See [Pagination](/docs/pagination) for numbered and cursor pages, query binding and data-source delegates.

## The client

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
import { InfiniteScroll } from '@inertiajs/react'

<InfiniteScroll data="posts">
  {posts.data.map((post) => <Post key={post.id} post={post} />)}
</InfiniteScroll>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { InfiniteScroll } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
import Post from './Post.vue'

defineProps<{ posts: { data: { id: number }[] } }>()
</script>

<template>
  <InfiniteScroll data="posts">
    <Post v-for="post in posts.data" :key="post.id" :post="post" />
  </InfiniteScroll>
</template>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { InfiniteScroll } from '@inertiajs/svelte'
  import Post from './Post.svelte'

  let { posts }: { posts: { data: { id: number }[] } } = $props()
</script>

<InfiniteScroll data="posts">
  {#each posts.data as post (post.id)}
    <Post {post} />
  {/each}
</InfiniteScroll>
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Metadata

`ScrollMetadata(PageName, PreviousPage, NextPage, CurrentPage)` is a record. Page values can be `int`, `long`, `string` or `null`. Cursor paging uses strings.

Metadata comes from the `metadata:` argument, or from the value if it implements `IProvidesScrollMetadata`. Without either, the render throws an exception with a message that names the prop.

```csharp
["posts"] = Scroll(page, wrapper: "data", metadata: ScrollMetadata.FromPage(2, hasMore: true)),
```

The client sends `X-Inertia-Infinite-Scroll-Merge-Intent: prepend` when scrolling up. The wrapper is then reported under `prependProps` instead of `mergeProps`.

`scrollProps[path].reset` is true when the request lists the path in `X-Inertia-Reset`.

## Combining with other props

`Scroll(...)` accepts the five loader shapes. You can combine it with `.Defer()`, `.Once()` and `.Rescue()`:

```csharp
["posts"] = Scroll(ct => feed.PageAsync(1, ct)).Defer(),
```

A deferred scroll prop reports `"posts.data"` in the same way as a resolved one. This behavior deliberately fixes an inertia-laravel quirk.

<Callout type="tip" title="Keep pages small">
Infinite scroll also limits the payload size. Load 10 to 20 items per page instead of sending an unbounded list on the first request.
</Callout>

---

# Pagination

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/pagination

> Create numbered and cursor pages for pagers and infinite scroll.

A long list is easier to browse when the server sends a small group of items at a time. A numbered page lets readers choose a page. A cursor page uses a marker to fetch the next or previous group. Start with a list already in memory:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia();
var app = builder.Build();
app.UseInertia();

// posts is an IReadOnlyList<PostDto> in a stable order.
app.MapGet("/posts", (PageRequest request) => Render("Posts/Index", new InertiaProps
{
    ["posts"] = Pagination.Paginate(posts, request),
}));
```

A visit to `/posts?page=2&perPage=5` returns the second group in `posts.data`. The default page size is 20 and the maximum is 100. Configure both in [Pagination options](/docs/configuration#opagination-paginationoptions). To stop at a last page, set `MaxPage` there. A page beyond `MaxPage` is empty and runs no query or count. For infinite scroll, wrap the page value in `Scroll(...)` and render it with `InfiniteScroll`, as shown in [Infinite scroll](/docs/infinite-scroll).

`Pagination` creates page values. `Scroll` adds infinite-scroll metadata and merging. Use a page directly for a classic pager.

| You write | You get |
|---|---|
| `Pagination.Paginate(posts, request)` | A numbered `Page<T>` for a pager |
| `Scroll(Pagination.Paginate(posts, request))` | Numbered infinite scroll |
| `Scroll(await Pagination.PaginateAsync(request, key, fetch, ct: ct))` | Cursor-based infinite scroll using your data source |
| `Scroll(ct => Pagination.PaginateAsync(request, fetch, ct: ct)).Defer()` | A deferred page. Other prop modifiers also work |

Minimal API handlers can take `PageRequest` or `CursorRequest` directly, as in [Infinite scroll](/docs/infinite-scroll). MVC and FastEndpoints can call `PageRequest.From(Request.Query)` and `CursorRequest.From(HttpContext)`. Page numbers below 1 become 1. Invalid page sizes use the default, and sizes above the maximum are reduced to the maximum. Set defaults and parameter names with `o.Pagination` in `AddInertia`. `From` and `BindAsync` keep the query parameter name for the returned page. An explicit paginator name overrides that name.

`Pagination.Paginate` slices an `IReadOnlyList<T>` that is already in memory. For a database, search SDK or HTTP API, use `Pagination.PaginateAsync`. It accepts a `fetch(skip, take, ct)` delegate and an optional count delegate. It requests one extra item to determine `hasMore`. Without a count, `total` and `lastPage` are null. Delegate offsets above `int.MaxValue` return an empty page without calling `fetch`. The optional count still runs. Supply a stable, fully unique ordering to your data source. Pages do not contain URL links. For a classic pager, use `currentPage`, `lastPage`, and `pageName` to build links.

```json
{ "data": [ { "id": 21 } ], "currentPage": 2, "perPage": 20, "total": 95, "lastPage": 5, "from": 21, "to": 40, "hasMore": true, "pageName": "page" }
```

`from` and `to` are one-based. Both are null on an empty page. The examples shorten the data array.

For example, a data source can implement numbered pages without exposing `IQueryable`:

```csharp
var page = await Pagination.PaginateAsync(
    request,
    (skip, take, ct) => store.FetchPostsAsync(skip, take, ct),
    ct => store.CountPostsAsync(ct),
    ct: cancellationToken);
```

For a pager, use Inertia links and preserve any other filters your app needs:

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
import { Link } from '@inertiajs/react'

{page.lastPage != null && Array.from({ length: page.lastPage }, (_, i) => i + 1).map((n) => (
  <Link key={n} href={`?${page.pageName}=${n}`} aria-current={n === page.currentPage ? 'page' : undefined}>
    {n}
  </Link>
))}
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Link } from '@inertiajs/vue3'

defineProps<{ page: { currentPage: number; lastPage: number | null; pageName: string } }>()
</script>

<template>
  <template v-if="page.lastPage != null">
    <Link
      v-for="n in page.lastPage"
      :key="n"
      :href="`?${page.pageName}=${n}`"
      :aria-current="n === page.currentPage ? 'page' : undefined"
    >
      {{ n }}
    </Link>
  </template>
</template>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Link } from '@inertiajs/svelte'

  let { page }: { page: { currentPage: number; lastPage: number | null; pageName: string } } = $props()
</script>

{#if page.lastPage != null}
  {#each Array.from({ length: page.lastPage }, (_, i) => i + 1) as n (n)}
    <Link href={`?${page.pageName}=${n}`} aria-current={n === page.currentPage ? 'page' : undefined}>
      {n}
    </Link>
  {/each}
{/if}
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Cursors

A cursor is a marker for the position of an item. Cursors are useful when readers move forward and backward rather than jump to page numbers. The cursor overload of `PaginateAsync` takes a key selector and a fetch delegate. The delegate receives:

- a decoded cursor with `Direction` (`After` or `Before`) and `Value`
- a take count
- a cancellation token

Return rows in the requested direction, including up to one extra. The helper trims and reverses `Before` results to display order. Choose a stable, unique, non-null key. `hasMore` indicates that there are more rows in the requested direction.

```json
{ "data": [ { "id": 21 } ], "perPage": 20, "nextCursor": "eyJ...", "previousCursor": null, "hasMore": true, "cursorName": "cursor" }
```

A cursor is the URL-safe base64 form of a compact JSON array: the direction (`"a"` or `"b"`) followed by the key values. Supported keys are `int`, `long`, `Guid`, `string`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `decimal`, `double`, and `bool`. Cursors are **not tamper-proof**. Apps that need tamper protection should wrap cursors with `IDataProtector`.

A malformed or foreign nonempty cursor falls back to the first page. When `CursorRequest.Logger` is set, the paginator logs the fallback at Debug, without cursor values or exception details. Minimal API binding uses the configured pagination options. It also supplies a logger in the `Inertia.Net.Pagination` category when a logger factory is available. In MVC or FastEndpoints, `CursorRequest.From(HttpContext)` does the same. Optional arguments override the configured defaults and parameter names. For a query-only request or a request created outside HTTP, supply an app logger explicitly:

```csharp
var request = CursorRequest.From(query) with { Logger = logger };
```

`Logger` is ignored by JSON serialization and does not affect request equality.

## Defer or cache a page

A page can use the same prop modifiers as other values. For example, `Scroll(ct => Pagination.PaginateAsync(request, fetch, ct: ct)).Defer()` loads the page after the first response. A lazy prop can also use `.Cache(...)`. See [Deferred props](/docs/deferred-props) and [Props](/docs/props) for loader and cache options.

## With EF Core

If your app uses EF Core, install the optional package alongside your database provider:

```sh
dotnet add package Inertia.Net.EntityFrameworkCore --version 1.9.8
```

The following example uses an existing `AppDb` as `db`, with a `Posts` set. `request` is a `PageRequest`, `cursorRequest` is a `CursorRequest`, and `ct` is the request cancellation token:

```csharp
using Inertia.Net;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

// Numbered pages: order first, including a unique tie-breaker if needed.
var page = await db.Posts.OrderByDescending(p => p.Id)
    .ToPageAsync(request, ct: ct);

// Cursor pages: pass an unordered query. The helper applies the ordering.
var cursorPage = await db.Posts
    .ToCursorPageAsync(p => p.CreatedAt, p => p.Id, cursorRequest,
        descending: true, ct: ct);

return Render("Feed", new InertiaProps { ["posts"] = Scroll(cursorPage) });
```

Both results contain the selected group in `data`. A cursor is a marker. Send it back unchanged to request the next or previous group. `ToPageAsync` requires an ordered query and counts rows by default. To skip the count, pass `countTotal: false`. Then `total` and `lastPage` are null. `ToCursorPageAsync` rejects a query that is already ordered. It orders by the supplied key and optional tie-breaker itself. Both guards throw `InvalidOperationException`. The cursor helper fetches in both directions without counting.

Choose a stable, fully unique ordering. Use a unique key, or add a unique tie-breaker when the first key can repeat. Nullable keys are not supported. The cursor codec supports the types listed above, but EF translation and ordering for each type depend on the database provider. For example, SQLite needs a suitable value conversion to order `DateTimeOffset`. The corresponding page parameter uses the name from a bound request or `From(...)`. An explicit `pageName` or `cursorName` argument takes precedence.

The EF Core package is not marked Native AOT compatible. EF Core has its own compiled-model requirements. For Native AOT applications, use the core delegate paginators with an AOT-compatible data source instead.

## With MongoDB

`Inertia.Net.MongoDB` builds the same `Page<T>` and `CursorPage<T>` values from a `collection.Find(filter)`:

```sh
dotnet add package Inertia.Net.MongoDB --version 1.9.8
```

```csharp
["users"] = await users.Find(u => u.Active).SortBy(u => u.Name).ThenBy(u => u.Id)
    .ToPageAsync(PageRequest.From(http.Request.Query), ct: ct),
["feed"] = Scroll(await posts.Find(p => p.Published)
    .ToCursorPageAsync(p => p.CreatedAt, p => p.Id, CursorRequest.From(http), descending: true, ct: ct)),
```

The rules are the same as for the EF Core helpers:

- `ToPageAsync` needs a sorted find. It replaces skip and limit, and counts the filter with `CountDocuments` unless you pass `countTotal: false`.
- `ToCursorPageAsync` needs an unsorted find. It adds the keyset condition to the find's filter and sorts by the key (and tie-breaker). Keys may be `ObjectId` (held in the cursor as its 24-character string), `int`, `long`, `string`, `Guid`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `decimal`, `double` or `bool`. A tampered or unparseable cursor starts at the first page.
- MongoDB orders strings by their UTF-8 bytes.

The MongoDB driver does not support trimming or Native AOT, so neither does this package. See the [package README](https://github.com/adzamkomladev/Inertia.Net/blob/main/src/Inertia.Net.MongoDB/README.md).

## Native AOT

Register each closed page type in your app's `JsonSerializerContext` along with the item types:

```csharp
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Page<PostDto>))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(CursorPage<PostDto>))]
```

See [Native AOT](/docs/native-aot).

## Caching and scroll props

A cached page still writes its scroll metadata. Use cache keys that include the page or cursor and all user or tenant dependencies. `Scroll(...)` can be deferred or cached. Do not reuse its mutable prop instance across requests. You cannot combine root `Append()` and `Prepend()` on the same prop. See [Props](/docs/props#cached-props) and [Infinite scroll](/docs/infinite-scroll).

### Project MongoDB lists into a DTO

Use `ToProjectedPageAsync` after `Project` when the view needs only a few fields. The sort and count still apply to the source query, and the page holds the projected type.

```csharp
var page = await articles.Find(a => a.Published)
    .SortBy(a => a.Id)
    .Project(a => new ArticleSummary(a.Id, a.Title))
    .ToProjectedPageAsync(request, ct: ct);
```

---

# Live props

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/live-props

> Props that refresh themselves when the server broadcasts an event.

A live prop refreshes itself when the server broadcasts an event. The page response says which props listen to which events. The client subscribes to the channels of those events. When an event arrives, the client reloads the affected props or applies the values the event carries. Your components never subscribe or clean up.

Three pieces make it work:

1. **An event**, defined once as a `LiveEvent` and shared by both sides.
2. **A prop marked `.Live(event)`**, which puts its listeners in the page's `liveProps`.
3. **A publish** through `IInertiaLive`, delivered to subscribers by a transport.

<Callout type="info" title="Client version">
Live props need `@inertiajs/react`, `@inertiajs/vue3` or `@inertiajs/svelte` 3.11.0 or later. Older clients ignore `liveProps`.
</Callout>

<Sequence
  caption="Figure: an event published on the server refreshes only the props that listen to it."
  actors={[
    { name: 'Your code', sub: 'IInertiaLive.Publish' },
    { name: 'Live transport', sub: 'SignalR or your own' },
    { name: 'Browser', sub: 'Inertia client' },
  ]}
  messages={[
    { from: 2, to: 1, text: 'Page loads, then subscribes to the channels in liveProps', code: '"liveProps": { "stats": ["orders.changed"] }', phase: 'Subscribe' },
    { from: 0, to: 1, text: 'Publish an event', code: 'live.PublishAsync(new OrderChanged(id))', phase: 'Event' },
    { from: 1, to: 2, text: 'Deliver it to every subscriber', reply: true },
    { from: 2, to: 1, text: 'Partial reload of only the affected props', code: 'X-Inertia-Partial-Data: stats', phase: 'Refresh' },
    { from: 2, to: 2, text: 'Component re-renders with fresh data' },
  ]}
/>

## Define each event once

A `LiveEvent` is an event name on a `LiveChannel`. You use the same `LiveEvent` value to declare the prop and to publish the event, so the two sides always match.

```csharp
public static class OrderEvents
{
    public static LiveEvent Updated(int id) => new("OrderUpdated", LiveChannel.Private($"orders.{id}"));
    public static LiveEvent StatsChanged { get; } = new("StatsChanged", LiveChannel.Public("stats"));
}
```

A channel is `LiveChannel.Public`, `Private`, `Presence` or `EncryptedPrivate`. Channel names carry no prefix. A transport adds `private-` or `presence-` itself when its protocol needs one.

## Mark props live

```csharp
app.MapGet("/orders/{id:int}", (int id, AppDb db) => Render("Orders/Show", new InertiaProps
{
    ["order"]   = Prop(ct => db.Orders.SingleAsync(o => o.Id == id, ct))
                      .Live(OrderEvents.Updated(id))
                      .Throttle(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500)),
    ["metrics"] = Defer(ct => metrics.ForOrderAsync(id, ct)).Live(OrderEvents.Updated(id)),
    ["stats"]   = Optional(() => stats.Today()).Live(OrderEvents.StatsChanged),
}));
```

The page lists every listener, including the listeners of props it left out:

```json
{
  "props": { "errors": {}, "order": { "id": 1, "status": "paid" } },
  "deferredProps": { "default": ["metrics"] },
  "liveProps": {
    "order": {
      "listeners": [
        { "channel": { "name": "orders.1", "type": "private" }, "events": ["OrderUpdated"] }
      ],
      "throttle": 500
    },
    "metrics": {
      "listeners": [
        { "channel": { "name": "orders.1", "type": "private" }, "events": ["OrderUpdated"] }
      ]
    },
    "stats": {
      "listeners": [
        { "channel": { "name": "stats", "type": "public" }, "events": ["StatsChanged"] }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

| Call | Effect |
|---|---|
| `.Live(event)` | Adds a listener. Repeatable: call it once per event. |
| `.Live(channel, "Created", "Deleted")` | Listens to several events on one channel. |
| `Live(() => ..., event)` | The factory form of `Prop(...).Live(event)`. |
| `.Throttle(window)` | The shortest time between two reloads of the prop. The client's default is one second. |

### What combines with live

| Prop | Live? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Prop`, `Always`, shared props | Yes | |
| `Defer`, `Optional` | Yes | Listeners are reported even while the value is left out. |
| `Once` | Yes | A once prop the client already holds stays subscribed. |
| `Rescue`, `Parallel` | Yes | A rescued prop stays subscribed. The next event fetches it again. |
| `Cache` | Yes | Publishing does not evict the cache. Remove the entry with `IInertiaCache` first. |
| `Merge`, `DeepMerge`, `Scroll` | No | A live prop is replaced whole, so these throw `InvalidOperationException`. Reload them from the page instead: see [Reloading scroll and merge props](#reloading-scroll-and-merge-props). |

A live prop inside an array reloads its whole array, as every [partial reload](/docs/partial-reloads) of an array descendant does. Prefer keyed objects for lists that change often.

## Shared live props

A shared live prop keeps something current on every page, such as a notification bell:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o => o.Share("notifications", ctx =>
{
    var userId = ctx.User.FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier);
    return userId is null ? null : Prop(ct => notifications.SummaryAsync(userId, ct))
        .Live(new LiveEvent("NotificationCreated", LiveChannel.Private($"users.{userId}")));
}));
```

## Publish events

`AddInertiaLive()` registers `IInertiaLive`, the service you publish events through. A transport registers the `IInertiaLiveBroadcaster` that delivers what `IInertiaLive` publishes.

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertiaLive();   // then a transport: .AddSignalR() or your own IInertiaLiveBroadcaster
```

<Tabs>
<Tab label="Reload">

```csharp
// Everyone else on the channel reloads `order`; the caller already has the response.
app.MapPost("/orders/{id:int}/ship", async (int id, HttpContext context, IInertiaLive live) =>
{
    await orders.ShipAsync(id);
    await live.PublishAsync(OrderEvents.Updated(id), exceptSocketId: context.InertiaRequest().SocketId);
    return Back();
});
```

</Tab>
<Tab label="With values">

```csharp
// Clients apply the value without a request; live props left out are reloaded.
await live.PublishAsync(OrderEvents.Updated(order.Id), new { order = OrderDto.From(order) });
```

</Tab>
<Tab label="Explicit metadata">

```csharp
// Written with that context's own options, as JsonSerializer would.
await live.PublishAsync(OrderEvents.Updated(order.Id), new OrderProps(dto), AppJsonContext.Default.OrderProps);
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

- **Without values**, every client reloads the live props that listen to the event, each with its own request and its own data.
- **With values**, the props named in the values are updated in place. The values are keyed by prop path (`"auth.user"` stays a flat key). Values use the page serializer options, so they match what a reload returns. Under Native AOT, the type needs to be in your registered JSON context, like any prop type.
- **`exceptSocketId`** leaves one connection out, usually the client that made the change. The client sends its id as `X-Socket-Id`, and `HttpContext.InertiaRequest().SocketId` reads it. The client supplies the header, so it is only ever used to exclude a connection.

<Callout type="danger" title="Every subscriber sees the same values">
A broadcast reaches every client on the channel. Only publish values that everyone allowed on the channel may see. When a value depends on the user, publish without values and let each client reload its own data.
</Callout>

A broadcaster delivers this payload:

```json
{
  "__inertia": {
    "event": "OrderUpdated",
    "props": { "order": { "id": 1, "status": "shipped" } }
  }
}
```

## Resolve values for a broadcast

Use plain values with `IInertiaLive.PublishAsync` when you already have the data. If you have prop definitions instead,
resolve them first. This handler fragment assumes `http`, `orders`, `id`, `live`, `orderUpdated` and `ct` are in scope:

```csharp
var values = await BroadcastPropsAsync(http, new InertiaProps
{
    ["order"] = Prop(ct => orders.FindAsync(id, ct)),
    ["stats.total"] = Defer(() => 42),
});
await live.PublishAsync(orderUpdated, values, exceptSocketId: http.InertiaRequest().SocketId, cancellationToken: ct);
```

Visit filters do not restrict a broadcast. Optional, deferred and once values all resolve. A rescued value is left out.
Dot-path keys stay flat. No page or DevTools entry is created.
Only publish values that every subscriber of the channel is allowed to see.

## On the client

Read a live prop like any other prop. `useProp` exposes the prop's loading state. The `live` router event is cancelable, so a listener can hold an update back, for example to show a "new posts" button instead:

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
import { router, useProp } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'

type Order = { id: number; status: string }

export default function Show() {
  const order = useProp<Order>('order')   // { value, loading, loaded }
  const [newPosts, setNewPosts] = useState(false)

  // Returning false holds the update back.
  useEffect(
    () =>
      router.on('live', (event) => {
        if (event.detail.props.includes('posts')) {
          setNewPosts(true)
          return false
        }
      }),
    [],
  )

  return (
    <>
      <p>Status: {order.value?.status}{order.loading && ' (updating...)'}</p>
      {newPosts && <button onClick={() => router.reload({ only: ['posts'] })}>New posts</button>}
    </>
  )
}
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { router, useProp } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
import { onUnmounted, ref } from 'vue'

type Order = { id: number; status: string }

const order = useProp<Order>('order')   // { value, loading, loaded }, each a ref
const newPosts = ref(false)

// Returning false holds the update back.
onUnmounted(
  router.on('live', (event) => {
    if (event.detail.props.includes('posts')) {
      newPosts.value = true
      return false
    }
  }),
)
</script>

<template>
  <p>Status: {{ order.value.value?.status }}<template v-if="order.loading.value"> (updating...)</template></p>
  <button v-if="newPosts" @click="router.reload({ only: ['posts'] })">New posts</button>
</template>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { router, useProp } from '@inertiajs/svelte'

  type Order = { id: number; status: string }

  const order = useProp<Order>('order')   // { value, loading, loaded }
  let newPosts = $state(false)

  // Returning false holds the update back.
  $effect(() =>
    router.on('live', (event) => {
      if (event.detail.props.includes('posts')) {
        newPosts = true
        return false
      }
    }),
  )
</script>

<p>Status: {order.value?.status}{order.loading ? ' (updating...)' : ''}</p>
{#if newPosts}
  <button onclick={() => router.reload({ only: ['posts'] })}>New posts</button>
{/if}
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## SignalR

`Inertia.Net.Live.SignalR` runs the transport inside your app. It provides:

- a SignalR hub the browser subscribes to
- channel authorization
- the broadcaster that `IInertiaLive` publishes through

```sh
dotnet add package Inertia.Net.Live.SignalR
npm install @microsoft/signalr # or: bun add, pnpm add, yarn add @microsoft/signalr
```

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertiaLive().AddSignalR(o =>
    o.Authorize((context, channel, ct) =>
        ValueTask.FromResult(channel.Name == $"users.{context.UserIdentifier}")));

var app = builder.Build();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();
app.UseInertia();
app.MapInertiaLiveHub();   // /inertia-live
```

Apps created with `dotnet new inertia` ship the client transport as `ClientApp/lib/inertia-signalr.ts`. In other apps, copy [the file](https://github.com/adzamkomladev/Inertia.Net/blob/main/src/Inertia.Net.Templates/content/common/ClientApp/lib/inertia-signalr.ts) into your app. Then turn the transport on:

```ts
import { signalr } from './lib/inertia-signalr'

createInertiaApp({ live: signalr() })
```

`@microsoft/signalr` loads on the first subscription, so pages without live props never download it. When a dropped connection comes back, the transport joins its channels again. Inertia then reloads every live prop once, which catches up on missed events.

### Who may join a channel

| Channel | Who joins |
|---|---|
| `Public` | Anyone who reaches the hub. Set `o.AuthorizePublicChannels = true` to ask the authorizer too. |
| `Private`, `Presence`, `EncryptedPrivate` | Only connections the authorizer allows. With no authorizer, nobody joins. |

For rules that need services, implement `ILiveChannelAuthorizer` and register it with `o.Authorize<OrderChannelAuthorizer>()`. The authorizer is created for each subscription, with constructor injection. SignalR has no presence member lists or end-to-end encryption, so presence and encrypted-private channels are authorized like private ones.

The hub answers requests from other origins with 403. Add trusted origins to `o.AllowedOrigins`. The origin check takes the place of antiforgery tokens on the hub. Connections close when their authentication expires.

<Callout type="warning" title="More than one server">
SignalR groups exist on one server only. When you run several instances, add a Redis backplane (`AddSignalR().AddStackExchangeRedis(...)`) or Azure SignalR Service. Without one of these, a publish reaches only the clients connected to the instance that sent it.
</Callout>

The [package README](https://github.com/adzamkomladev/Inertia.Net/blob/main/src/Inertia.Net.Live.SignalR/README.md) lists the client options, how channels map to SignalR groups, and the security notes.

## Reloading scroll and merge props

A `Scroll(...)` or `Merge(...)` prop cannot be live, because a live reload would merge the reloaded page into the list. Reload such a prop from the page instead, with `ClientApp/lib/inertia-live-reload.ts`, which `dotnet new inertia` apps include:

```csharp
o.TypeScript.RoutesOutputPath = "ClientApp/types/routes.ts";
o.TypeScript.LiveEvents(Events.PostCreated);   // exported from routes.ts as liveEvents.PostCreated
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
import { useEffect } from 'react'
import { liveReload } from '../lib/inertia-live-reload'
import { live } from '../lib/live'                 // the value given to createInertiaApp({ live })
import { liveEvents } from '../types/routes'

useEffect(() => liveReload(live, liveEvents.PostCreated, { only: ['posts'], reset: ['posts'] }), [])
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, onUnmounted } from 'vue'
```
