# Configuration

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/configuration

> InertiaOptions, Vite, SSR, props, state and the middleware and result API.

Pass core configuration to `AddInertia`. Pass error page options to `AddInertiaErrorPages`. Options marked “Development only” do nothing in other environments.

`ComponentTransformer` changes runtime component names only. If you use it, also register the final client names for TypeScript
generation, because a build cannot evaluate an arbitrary runtime callback.

## `AddInertia(o => ...)`: `InertiaOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RootView` | `"app.html"` | Root template path, relative to the content root. With `UseRazorRootView`, a Razor view name. Paths outside the content root are refused. |
| `RootElementId` | `"app"` | Id of the root element and the `data-page` script. |
| `Version` | `null` | Asset version. `null` means the Vite manifest hash, or `""` without one. |
| `VersionResolver` | `null` | `Func<HttpContext, string?>` that returns the version for each request. Takes priority over `Version` when non-null. |
| `ComponentTransformer` | `null` | Changes the component name before rendering and page-file checks. Returning null keeps the name. |
| `EncryptHistory` | `false` | Encrypt browser history state of every page. |
| `WithAllErrors` | `false` | Send every validation message per field instead of the first. |
| `PreserveBigIntegers` | `false` | Emit integers beyond ±(2^53−1) as `{"$bigint":"..."}`. |
| `ExposeSharedPropKeys` | `true` | List top-level shared keys in `sharedProps`. |
| `CspNonce` | `null` | `Func<HttpContext, string?>`: the request's CSP nonce. |
| `ConvertExternalRedirects` | `true` | Turn an Inertia redirect to another origin into `409` + `X-Inertia-Location`. |
| `UrlResolver` | `null` | `Func<HttpContext, string>`: the page `url`. |
| `Pages.Directory` / `Pages.Extensions` | `null` / `.tsx .jsx .ts .js .vue .svelte` | Development check that a rendered component has a page file. |
| `TypeScript.OutputPath`, `.Page<T>(component)`, `.SharedProps<T>()`, `.FlashData<T>()` | `null` | TypeScript declarations, written in Development. |
| `Share(key, value)` / `Share(key, Func<HttpContext, object?>)` | none | Shared props. |

## `o.Pagination`: `PaginationOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DefaultPerPage` | `20` | Default page size. |
| `MaxPerPage` | `100` | Maximum page size. Must be below `int.MaxValue` to allow over-fetching. The default page size must be between 1 and this value. |
| `MaxPage` | `null` | The last numbered page a bound `PageRequest` may fetch. A page beyond it is empty and runs no query or count. `null` means no ceiling. |
| `PageName` | `"page"` | Numbered-page query parameter. |
| `PerPageName` | `"perPage"` | Page-size query parameter. |
| `CursorName` | `"cursor"` | Cursor query parameter. |

## `o.Vite`: `ViteOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PublicDirectory` | `"wwwroot"` | Web root containing the build directory and hot file. |
| `BuildDirectory` | `"build"` | Vite output directory under `PublicDirectory`. Also the URL prefix. |
| `ManifestPath` | `null` | Manifest path relative to the content root. `null` means `{PublicDirectory}/{BuildDirectory}/.vite/manifest.json`, then `manifest.json`. |
| `HotFilePath` | `null` | Hot file path relative to the content root. `null` means `{PublicDirectory}/hot`. Read in Development only. |
| `DevServerUrl` | `null` | Dev server origin, for example `http://localhost:5173`. When set, dev tags always render. |
| `AssetBaseUrl` | `null` | Replaces `{PathBase}/{BuildDirectory}` as the URL prefix of built assets. |
| `Prefetch` | `None` | `Waterfall` or `Aggressive`: prefetch code-split chunks after load. |
| `PrefetchConcurrency` | `3` | Chunks `Waterfall` downloads at a time. |

## `o.Ssr`: `SsrOptions`

`Ssr.ConnectTimeout` limits how long opening a connection may take, separately from the rendering deadline. The default is five seconds. Use a positive supported duration or `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan`.

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Mode` | `Disabled` | `Disabled`, `Preferred` or `Required`. `Disabled` cannot be overridden per response. |
| `OnRenderFailed` | `null` | Thread-safe `Action<SsrRenderFailed>` called once for the final failed render attempt, before fallback or a Required-mode exception. |
| `Urls` | empty (`http://127.0.0.1:13714`) | SSR server base URLs. Not used with `UseNodeProcess()`. |
| `Timeout` | `5 s` | Total deadline per render. `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` disables it. |
| `MaxResponseBytes` | `16 MiB` | Limit on actual response bytes, including errors and chunked responses. |
| `MaxPageBytes` | `2 MiB` | Pages whose JSON is larger render on the client without a call. |
| `BundlePath` | `null` | Skip SSR while this file is missing, unless the Vite dev server runs. |
| `ExcludePaths` | empty | Request paths never rendered on the server (exact, or a trailing `*` for a prefix). |
| `Concurrency.MaxActive` | `8` | Renders in flight per server from this app instance. `0` means no limit. |
| `Concurrency.MaxQueued` | `32` | Renders waiting for a slot per server. |
| `Concurrency.QueueTimeout` | `250 ms` | How long a render waits for a slot. |
| `CircuitBreaker.Enabled` | `true` | Pause servers that keep failing. |
| `CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold` | `5` | Consecutive failures that open a server's circuit. |
| `CircuitBreaker.BreakDuration` | `10 s` | How long an open circuit skips the server before one probe. |
| `Cache.Duration` | `Zero` (off) | Reuse a render for this long when the page JSON is the same. |
| `Cache.StaleFor` | `Zero` | Serve stale while re-rendering. |
| `Cache.MaxBytes` | `64 MiB` | Size of the default store's render cache. |
| `UseNodeProcess(configure?)` | off | Start and supervise Node SSR processes. Sets `Mode = Preferred` when the mode is `Disabled`. |

To set SSR for one response, use `Render(...).WithSsr(SsrMode)` or `.WithoutSsr()`. The full SSR options are in [Server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering).

## `o.Props`: `InertiaPropsOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MaxConcurrency` | `4` | Loaders marked `.Parallel()` that run at once per render. Must be positive. |
| `CacheMaxBytes` | `null` | Size of the default store's cached props. When set, cached props go in a private cache and the least recently used are evicted. `null` keeps them in the app's `IMemoryCache` without a bound of their own. |

## `o.State`: `InertiaStateOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CookieName` | `".Inertia.State"` | Cookie name (cookie store) or session key (session store). |
| `RememberPreviousUrl` | `false` | Remember successful page GET URLs for `Back()` when Referer is unavailable. |
| `RememberPartialReloads` | `false` | Also remember same-component partial reload URLs when previous-URL tracking is enabled. Non-Inertia AJAX, prefetch and Precognition requests remain excluded. |
| `PreviousUrlCookieName` | `".Inertia.Previous"` | Plain previous-URL cookie, used with either state store. Must be non-empty and different from `CookieName`. |
| `CookieSecurePolicy` | `SameAsRequest` | When state and previous-URL cookies are `Secure`. |
| `UseSession()` | off | Use `ISession` instead of the encrypted cookie. |
| `AddInertiaMvc(o => o.UseTempDataStateStore())` | off | Use MVC TempData. Requires the Inertia.Net.Mvc package. |

## `AddInertiaErrorPages(o => ...)`: `InertiaErrorPagesOptions`

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Component` | `"Error"` | Default error component. |
| `Components` | empty | Per-status overrides, with keys in `StatusCodes`. |
| `StatusCodes` | `[403, 404, 500, 503]` | Non-empty set of statuses from 400 to 599. Protocol `409` and antiforgery `419` responses are preserved. |
| `EnabledInDevelopment` | `false` | Preview error components in Development. |
| `Props` | `null` | `Func<HttpContext, int, Exception?, InertiaProps>` for additional props. |

See [Error pages](/docs/error-pages) for setup, shared props and existing exception middleware.

## Middleware and endpoint API

| API | Description |
|---|---|
| `services.AddInertia(configure?)` | Registers services and options. |
| `services.AddInertiaErrorPages(configure?)` / `app.UseInertiaErrorPages(useExceptionHandler: true)` | Error page services and middleware. Call the middleware before `UseInertia()`. Pass `false` when you use your own `UseExceptionHandler()`. |
| `app.UseInertia()` | The protocol middleware. Call it before the endpoints, and after `UseSession()` when used. |
| `app.UseInertiaAntiforgery(configure?)` | Issues the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie and validates unsafe requests (`419` on failure). |
| `app.MapInertia(pattern, component, props?)` | GET and HEAD endpoint that renders the component. |
| `services.AddInertiaDevTools(configure?)` / `app.MapInertiaDevTools()` | DevTools recorder and read API. Inertia.Net logs a warning when recording is enabled outside Development without an `Authorize` callback. The read API then returns 404. |
| `app.UseInertiaAntiforgeryCookie(cookieName = "XSRF-TOKEN")` | Only writes the token cookie. You validate the token yourself. |
| `endpoint.WithInertiaValidation()` | Minimal API: validation failures redirect back with errors. |
| `endpoint.WithInertiaPrecognition()` | Minimal API: `WithInertiaValidation()` plus Precognition. |
| `healthChecks.AddInertiaSsr(...)` | SSR health check from the gateway's state. |
| `mvc.AddInertiaMvc(o => o.UseRazorRootView("App"))` | MVC filter, optional Razor root view and component resolver. |
| `config.ConfigureInertia(configure?)` | FastEndpoints: validation redirect and Precognition. |
| `Render(component, props?)` | `InertiaResult`: `.WithStatusCode`, `.WithRootView`, `.WithViewData`, `.WithSsr`, `.WithoutSsr`, `.WithSsrCache`. |
| `Location(url)` | `InertiaLocationResult`. |
| `Back(fallback = "~/")` | `InertiaBackResult`: `.WithErrors`, `.WithFlash`. |
| `httpContext.Inertia()` | `InertiaFeature`: `Share`, `Flash`, `WithErrors`, `ClearHistory`, `EncryptHistory`, `PreserveFragment`. |
| `Send.InertiaAsync(...)`, `Send.InertiaLocationAsync(...)`, `Send.InertiaBackAsync(...)` | FastEndpoints `Send` extensions. |

## Extension points

- `IInertiaRootView`
- `IInertiaStateStore`
- `ViteAssets`
- `InertiaRequest` (parsed headers)
- `InertiaHeaders` (header name constants)
- `InertiaSsrException`
- `InertiaSsr.HttpClientName` (the SSR HTTP client)
- `InertiaDiagnostics` (meter and activity source names)

## Name collisions

The package imports `Inertia.Net` and static members of `Inertia.Net.Inertia` when implicit usings are enabled. If a name such as `Location` collides with a type, use `Inertia.Net.Inertia.Location(url)`. To manage imports yourself, set `<InertiaNetImplicitUsings>false</InertiaNetImplicitUsings>` in the project and add `using Inertia.Net;` and `using static Inertia.Net.Inertia;` where needed.

`InertiaPropJsonConverter`, `InertiaSsrHealthCheck`, `InertiaCacheEntryKind`, `InertiaCacheEntryOptions`, `InertiaPagesOptions`, `InertiaPrecognition.IsPrecognitive(...)` and `InertiaPrecognitionMetadata` are public APIs for serialization, health checks, cache stores, page checks and precognitive request handling.

---

# Testing

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/testing

> Fluent assertions over Inertia responses and helpers for partial reloads and deferred props.

`Inertia.Net.Testing` has Laravel-style fluent assertions over Inertia responses and `HttpClient` helpers. It parses both JSON responses (`X-Inertia: true`) and the first-visit HTML `<script data-page>`. It also decodes `$bigint` values. A failed assertion throws `InertiaAssertionException` with a readable message, so the package works with any test framework.

## Check page files and large integers

By default, `Component("Users/Index")` checks only the returned component name. To also check that the page file exists, use this fragment inside a test:

```csharp
var options = new InertiaTestingOptions { EnsurePagesExist = true };
options.PageDirectories.Add("ClientApp/pages"); // Use an absolute path if the test runs elsewhere.
var page = await response.GetInertiaPageAsync();
new AssertableInertia(page, options).Component("Users/Index");
```

React, Vue and Svelte extensions are allowed by default. Change `PageExtensions` to narrow that list.
`Component("Users/Index", false)` skips the file check. Passing `true` forces it.

When the page enables `preserveBigIntegers`, `Where` and `HasFlash` compare `$bigint` markers as integers,
including nested values. The raw page stays unchanged. Without that flag, markers remain ordinary objects.

A complete test class looks like this:

```csharp
using Inertia.Net.Testing;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;

public class UsersTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory) : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    // Keeps cookies (flash, errors) and does not follow redirects, so a test can assert the 303 itself.
    private readonly HttpClient _client = factory.CreateClient(new WebApplicationFactoryClientOptions
    {
        AllowAutoRedirect = false,
    });

    [Fact]
    public async Task Index_lists_users()
    {
        using var response = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/users");   // sends X-Inertia, X-Requested-With

        await response.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page
            .Component("Users/Index")
            .Url("/users")
            .Has("users", 3, first => first.Where("name", "Ann").WhereType("id", "integer").Etc())
            .Where("filters.search", "")
            .Missing("secret")
            .HasFlash("toast", "Welcome"));
    }
}
```

Add `public partial class Program;` to your app when it uses top-level statements.

To check that an error page keeps its HTTP status, use `Status` with the response's page assertion:

```csharp
using var response = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/missing");
await response.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page.Status(404).Component("Error"));
```

## Test host recipe

With `WebApplicationFactory<Program>`, pin the asset version so that requests need no first visit to learn it. Also turn SSR (server-side rendering) off so that tests need no Node server:

```csharp
builder.ConfigureTestServices(services => services.PostConfigure<InertiaOptions>(o =>
{
    o.Version = "test";              // then client.InertiaGetAsync(url, version: "test")
    o.Ssr.Mode = SsrMode.Disabled;
}));
```

For form posts, read the XSRF token from a page response with `GetXsrfToken()` and send it with `WithXsrfToken()`. See [Testing a form with antiforgery](#testing-a-form-with-antiforgery). A client that keeps cookies holds the antiforgery cookie and the sign-in cookie between requests. Create one with `factory.CreateClient(new() { AllowAutoRedirect = false, HandleCookies = true })`.

## Request helpers

| Helper | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `InertiaGetAsync(url, version?, configure?)` | Sends an Inertia GET |
| `InertiaRequestAsync(method, url, content?, version?, configure?)` | Sends an Inertia request with any method |
| `GetInertiaPageAsync()` | Parses the response into an `InertiaPage` |
| `AssertInertiaAsync(assert)` | Parses, runs the assertions and returns the page |

## Page assertions

The page assertions are:

- `Component`, `Url` and `Version`.
- `HasFlash(key)`, `HasFlash(key, value)` and `MissingFlash(key)`.
- `HasDeferred(path)` and `HasDeferred(group, path)`.
- `HasLive(path)` and `HasLive(path, channel, event)` for [live props](/docs/live-props). Write the channel as `"{type}:{name}"`, for example `private:orders.1`.
- `HasHead(key)` or `HasHead(key, contains)` for [head tags](/docs/head-tags). The key matches the tags' `data-inertia` attribute: `title`, a meta name or property, or a link rel.

For example:

```csharp
await response.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page.HasHead("title", "Users - App").HasHead("description"));
```

## Prop assertions

These assertions work on props and nested scopes. Keys can use dot paths and array indexes:

`Has(key)`, `Has(key, count)`, `Has(key, scope)`, `Has(key, count, firstItemScope)`, `HasAll`, `HasAny`, `Missing`, `MissingAll`, `Where(key, value)`, `Where(key, predicate)`, `WhereNot`, `WhereNull`, `WhereNotNull`, `WhereType(key, "string|null")`, `WhereAllType`, `WhereContains(key, ...)`, `Count`, `CountBetween`, `Each(scope)`, `First(scope)` and `Dump()`.

`WhereRoute(key, url, method)` asserts a route sent as a prop in the client's `{ url, method }` shape. The generated [`routes.ts`](/docs/typed-routes) functions return that shape. The method defaults to `get`, and the comparison ignores case:

```csharp
await response.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page.WhereRoute("actions.delete", "/users/1", "delete"));
```

**Strict interaction tracking.** Like Laravel, a nested scope fails when it contains properties you did not assert, unless you end the scope with `Etc()`. The root scope is not checked automatically. Call `.Interacted()` at the end to require that every top-level prop was asserted.

## Partial reloads and deferred props

`InertiaPage` replays the request with the right headers:

```csharp
var page = await (await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/dashboard")).GetInertiaPageAsync();

new AssertableInertia(page).HasDeferred("sidebar", "stats").Missing("stats");

var loaded = await page.LoadDeferredPropsAsync(_client, "sidebar");     // all groups when none are named
new AssertableInertia(loaded).Has("stats");

new AssertableInertia(page).HasScroll("posts");
var next = await page.LoadNextPageAsync(_client, "posts");
var previous = await next.LoadPreviousPageAsync(_client, "posts");

var only = await page.ReloadOnlyAsync(_client, "users");
var except = await page.ReloadExceptAsync(_client, "users");
```

`HasScroll(path)` asserts scroll metadata. `HasScroll(path, currentPage, nextPage)` also checks the page values. The next-page and previous-page helpers use the metadata and send the appropriate append or prepend intent.

`ReloadOnlyAsync` asserts that `"users"` is in the result. `ReloadExceptAsync` asserts that `"users"` is missing.

## InertiaPage members

`Props`, `Raw`, `Prop(path)`, `HasProp(path)`, `PropBigInteger(path)`, `DeferredProps`, `MergeProps`, `PrependProps`, `DeepMergeProps`, `MatchPropsOn`, `RescuedProps`, `SharedProps`, `ScrollProps`, `OnceProps`, `LiveProps`, `Flash`, `EncryptHistory`, `ClearHistory`, `PreserveFragment`, `PreserveBigIntegers`.

<Callout type="tip" title="Cookies and redirects">
Flash and errors travel in a cookie across the redirect, so use a client that keeps cookies. Disable `AllowAutoRedirect` to assert the redirect itself. Then follow the redirect with a second `InertiaGetAsync` to read the flash or errors.
</Callout>

## Testing a form with antiforgery

Keep cookies and disable redirects on the test client. Then:

1. Load the form.
2. Send the form's XSRF token on the Inertia POST.
3. Follow the redirect.

```csharp
using var formPage = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/users/create");
using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "/users")
{
    Content = JsonContent.Create(new { email = "" }),
};
request.Headers.Add("X-Inertia", "true");
request.Headers.Add("X-Requested-With", "XMLHttpRequest");
request.Headers.Referrer = new Uri(_client.BaseAddress!, "/users/create");
request.WithXsrfToken(formPage);
using var response = await _client.SendAsync(request);
Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Redirect, response.StatusCode);
using var redirected = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/users/create");
await redirected.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page.HasErrors().HasError("email"));
```

Import `System.Net` and `System.Net.Http.Json`. For a named error bag, use `HasErrorBag("createUser")` and `HasError("email", bag: "createUser")`. Dotted keys such as `items.0.email` are matched as flat error keys. With all errors enabled, a message assertion matches any message. `GetXsrfToken()` and `WithXsrfToken()` accept custom cookie and header names. The cookie container must keep the antiforgery cookie as well as the Inertia state cookie.

---

# DevTools

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/devtools

> Record visits for the Inertia DevTools extension and catch missing page components during development.

Inertia DevTools lets you see what your browser sent and what ASP.NET Core returned for an Inertia visit.

## Try it in the starter

DevTools lets you inspect a visit without changing its response. Its read API, the endpoints that return the recorded entries,
leaves pending errors and flash messages alone. Apps hosted under a path such as `/admin` report that path to the extension.
Request URLs are absolute. Sensitive query values are redacted in the recorded copy, not in your real request.

Entries live in memory and disappear on restart. Source-call locations are not collected, so some “open in editor” links
are unavailable. Keep the read API private, because recorded entries can include user data.

1. Install the browser extension using the [Inertia.js DevTools guide](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/advanced/devtools#installation).
2. Start the app and Vite from [First 10 minutes](/docs/first-10-minutes). Open `http://localhost:5180/todos`, open your browser's developer tools, and select the **Inertia** panel.
3. Submit an empty todo title. Select the visit in the timeline and look at the request and the resulting page data. The validation message is under `props.errors.title`.

The starter enables recording in Development. To add recording to an existing app, use the setup below.

## Enable DevTools

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertiaDevTools();   // records in Development only
app.UseInertia();
app.MapInertiaDevTools();                // GET /_inertia/devtools/entries/{id} and /entries
```

The list endpoint returns metadata summaries. Fetch `/entries/{id}` for props, HTTP bodies and route details.
Ordinary textual and JSON responses are captured up to `MaxResponseBytes`. Binary, explicitly streamed and oversized
responses are omitted. Parsed multipart forms include file names, sizes and MIME types, never file contents.
Unparsed uploads are not read only for recording. Render source locations are included when debug symbols are available.
Published or Native AOT applications may not retain them. Malformed structured bodies and invalid UTF-8 are omitted, because
a raw-text fallback could expose an unredacted secret.

To exclude paths, use `o.ExcludePaths.Add("/health")` or `o.ExcludePaths.Add("/assets/*")` in `AddInertiaDevTools(o => ...)`.
Untagged requests use the global entry/byte/age limits. `MaxEntriesPerTab` applies only when a browser tab ID is supplied.

Each request through `UseInertia()` gets an `X-Inertia-Devtools-Id` and an entry in memory. Entries are kept per browser tab, at most `MaxEntriesPerTab` and `MaxEntries`, for `MaxAge`. An entry holds:

- request type
- timings
- headers
- bodies
- the page object and its props metadata

The first page carries the discovery tag that the extension reads. In props, bodies and headers, DevTools replaces a value with `[REDACTED]` when its name contains `password`, `secret`, `token`, `authorization`, `cookie` or `api_key`. Add names with `RedactedKeys`. Nothing leaves the app.

Sensitive query parameters are also redacted in recorded request/page URLs, redirects and URL headers. Actual application URLs are unchanged. Malformed JSON bodies are omitted. Only eligible Inertia text bodies with a known length up to `MaxBodyBytes` are buffered. Unknown-length nonseekable bodies are omitted as streamed, so recording does not spool bulk requests to disk. A page larger than `MaxResponseBytes` is recorded without its body and is never copied. The default for `MaxResponseBytes` is 1 MiB. The entry is marked `too-large`, with the page size in `__meta.responseBytes`. The browser still receives the whole page. Kept entries are also bounded by `MaxTotalBytes`. The default for `MaxTotalBytes` is 64 MiB, and the oldest entries are dropped first.

Outside Development, nothing is recorded unless `Enabled = true`. Outside Development, the read API answers only requests that `Authorize` accepts. Other requests get `404`. With `Pages.Directory` set, entries link the component to its file.

## Page component check

To turn on the check, set `Pages.Directory`:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.Pages.Directory = "ClientApp/pages";   // Development only
    o.Pages.Extensions = [".tsx", ".vue"];   // optional
});
```

In Development, `Render` throws when the component has no page file. The message names the closest one:

```text
'Users/Indx' was not found in 'ClientApp/pages' ... Did you mean 'Users/Index'?
```

Names match exactly, as the client resolver does, even on case-insensitive file systems. Outside Development there is no check and no file access.

`Pages.Extensions` lists the file types. The default is `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.js`, `.vue` and `.svelte`.

## Generated TypeScript

The development startup also writes TypeScript declarations when `o.TypeScript.OutputPath` is set. The startup writes the file only when the content changed. See [TypeScript types](/docs/typescript).

## What to check before deploying

- `Pages.Directory` can stay configured. It is inactive outside Development.
- DevTools recording is off unless explicitly enabled.
- The generated TypeScript file is committed if the client build type-checks in CI.
- Production logs do not contain the DevTools read API.

Without an `Authorize` callback, the read API responds only in Development. Requests must come from this machine through a loopback connection to a loopback host name such as `localhost`. They must have no `X-Forwarded-For`, `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Real-IP` or `Via` header. Set `Authorize` to allow access from a container or another machine.

A reverse proxy on the same machine makes remote requests look local if it adds none of those headers. Set `Authorize` in that case too.

If recording is enabled outside Development without an `Authorize` callback, the app logs a warning and the read API returns 404. Map the read API with `MapInertiaDevTools()` and authorize its users.

The recorder's process-wide latch stays active after first use. The process-wide latch for parallel-prop planning does too.

---

# Troubleshooting

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/troubleshooting

> Common errors, their causes, and how to fix them.

## `Inertia.Render(...)` does not compile

The compiler reports `'Inertia' is a namespace`. Call `Render(...)` without a namespace or class prefix. The namespace `Inertia.Net` shadows the class name outside the `Inertia.Net` namespace.

The global usings come from the package's `buildTransitive` props and need `<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>`. Without implicit usings, or with `InertiaNetImplicitUsings` set to `false`, add `using static Inertia.Net.Inertia;`.

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem title="Generated code fails with 'Inertia' is a type">
    Inside a namespace that starts with `Inertia.Net.`, the name `Inertia` binds to the `Inertia.Net.Inertia` class. Source generators that emit non-`global::` names starting with `Inertia` then break. Do not put your app's code under an `Inertia.Net.*` namespace.
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Vite manifest not found. Looked in: ...">
    Do one of these three things. Run your package manager’s build script (`npm run build`, `bun run build`, `pnpm run build` or `yarn run build`). Or start the dev server so that the hot file exists in Development. Or set `o.Vite.ManifestPath` / `o.Vite.BuildDirectory`. Check that Vite writes `.vite/manifest.json` (`build.manifest: true`, Vite 5 and later) to `wwwroot/build`. Also check that the build output is part of what you deploy.
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Vite entry '...' was not found in the manifest">
    The `@vite("...")` argument must equal the manifest key, which is the path relative to the Vite root. The error lists the available entries.
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

## TypeLoadException for `IValidatableInfo` on .NET 11

`Could not load type 'Microsoft.Extensions.Validation.IValidatableInfo'` (or `ValidatableTypeInfo`) means a .NET 10 build is running on .NET 11. Upgrade every Inertia.Net package to 1.8.0 or later and target `net11.0`. Do not roll a `net10.0` app forward to the .NET 11 runtime. See [Installation](/docs/installation).

## My 404 shows the Inertia modal in production

Register `AddInertiaErrorPages()` and call `UseInertiaErrorPages()` before `UseInertia()`. Create your error components. See [Error pages](/docs/error-pages).

## Form submissions fail with 419

`UseInertiaAntiforgery()` rejected a request without a valid `X-XSRF-TOKEN`. Check these points:

- The page was loaded through the middleware. The middleware sets the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie.
- The cookie reaches the browser. A `Secure` cookie on plain HTTP is dropped. See [Deploying](/docs/deploying).
- All instances share the Data Protection key ring.
- `UseAuthentication()` runs before `UseInertiaAntiforgery()`.

A sign-in or sign-out changes the token. After one, reload the page, or return `Back()` from `OnRejected`. Exempt webhooks and token-authenticated APIs with `.DisableAntiforgery()` or `ShouldValidate`.

## The Inertia page component was not found

This error means that `o.Pages.Directory` is set and the component passed to `Render(...)` has no page file in that directory. Names match exactly, as the client's page resolver does, even on case-insensitive file systems. The message suggests the closest page. Fix the name, or check `Pages.Extensions` when your pages use another extension. The check runs only in Development.

## A redirect to another site turns into a 409

This is the `ConvertExternalRedirects` option, which is on by default. An Inertia request cannot follow a redirect to another origin. Instead, the request gets `409` + `X-Inertia-Location` and the client does a full visit.

If this happens for your own host, the app is behind a proxy that does not forward the scheme. See [Deploying](/docs/deploying), or use relative redirects. To disable the conversion, set `o.ConvertExternalRedirects = false`.

## The root view resolves outside the content root

`RootView` and `WithRootView(...)` take a path relative to the content root. Absolute paths and `..` are refused. Never derive these paths from request data.

## The page keeps reloading, or a request loops with 409

A `409` means the asset version differs between the client and the server. A loop means the two versions never match. Usually the version changes on every request: a `VersionResolver` returns a new value each time, or a file watcher regenerates the manifest. Another usual cause is that different instances behind a load balancer serve different builds. Use a stable version string.

In Development the manifest hash changes after each `vite build`, which is expected once.

## A blank page at localhost:5173

`http://localhost:5173` is the Vite dev server. It serves assets and hot-reload updates to your app. It has no pages of its own, so it shows a blank page. Instead, open the ASP.NET Core URL that `dotnet watch` or `dotnet run` prints. In the starter templates that URL is `http://localhost:5180`.

## The dev server tags do not appear

Inertia.Net reads the hot file only when `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development`. Check that `wwwroot/hot` exists and contains `http://localhost:5173`, or set `o.Vite.DevServerUrl`. Also set `base: '/'` for the dev server in `vite.config`.

## The root template was not found, or @inertia is missing

`RootView` is relative to the **content root**. Copy `app.html` to the output and publish directories (`CopyToOutputDirectory`, `CopyToPublishDirectory`). The template must contain `@inertia`.

## Flash data or errors disappear

Browsers limit the state cookie to about 4 KB. Flash less data, or use `o.State.UseSession()`. If the app runs on several instances, share Data Protection keys.

If the browser never sends the cookie back, check the cookie's `Secure` flag when the app runs on HTTP behind a proxy that does not forward `X-Forwarded-Proto`.

## Validation errors do not show up (Minimal API)

Use `.WithInertiaValidation()` on the endpoint. Without it, the built-in `AddValidation()` filter returns a `400` problem details response that the Inertia client cannot use. Make sure the model types are `public`.

## Validation keys do not match my field names

Keys use dotted indices and available JSON member aliases. Minimal API and MVC use the page serializer’s HTTP JSON options. FastEndpoints uses its binding serializer policy. Keep these aligned with client field names. Metadata-free or custom resolver paths can fall back to naming-policy conversion. See [Validation](/docs/validation-and-errors).

## InertiaProp values can only be serialized by Inertia.Net

An `InertiaProp` is in a place that Inertia.Net does not walk:

- a `Flash(...)` value
- a read-only dictionary type that does not implement `IDictionary`
- a type with a custom converter

Inertia.Net walks lists, typed dictionaries (`Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` with any key type), `object` members and `IDictionary<string, object?>`. Put props in `InertiaProps`, or declare the member as `InertiaProp` (or `object`) on the typed page object.

## Native AOT: JsonTypeInfo metadata was not provided

Add the type to your `JsonSerializerContext` and chain it with `ConfigureHttpJsonOptions`. To find these errors early, set `JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault=false` in regular builds. See [Native AOT](/docs/native-aot).

## SSR does not run and there is no error

SSR falls back to client rendering on any failure. Look for the warnings `Inertia SSR failed (...)` and `Inertia SSR skipped (...)`. The first includes the server's hint.

Check these points:

- `o.Ssr.Mode` and `Urls`.
- The Node server is running (`GET /health`). With `UseNodeProcess()`, look for `Inertia.Net.Ssr` log lines.
- `BundlePath` points at the built file.
- The path is not in `ExcludePaths`.
- The page is under `MaxPageBytes`.

To see the failure, set `Mode = SsrMode.Required` in Development.

## SSR skipped (circuit-open) or (overloaded)

- `circuit-open`: the server failed `CircuitBreaker.FailureThreshold` times in a row and is skipped for `BreakDuration`. The earlier `Inertia SSR failed` warnings say why.
- `overloaded`: more renders arrived than `Concurrency.MaxActive` plus `MaxQueued`, or one waited longer than `QueueTimeout`. Add servers or instances, or raise the limits if the server has spare capacity.

## Several managed instances never become healthy

Every instance must listen on its own port. For that, the SSR entry has to read `process.env.INERTIA_SSR_PORT`. A bundle built only by `@inertiajs/vite` listens on the port that was fixed at build time.

## The SSR output is not hydrated

Use the hydrating client entry shown in [Server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering) and build both bundles from the same sources. The SSR body is marked `data-server-rendered="true"`.

## Does it work behind a path base?

Yes. The page `url` keeps the path base, the Vite URLs include it, and `Back()` works.

## Can I use Newtonsoft.Json?

No. Props use System.Text.Json with the HTTP JSON options.

## Can I mix Razor Pages or views with Inertia pages?

Yes. Inertia handles only the endpoints that return `Render(...)`. The middleware leaves other responses alone, apart from `Vary: X-Inertia`.

## Forms submit invalid data

Minimal API endpoints need `.WithInertiaValidation()` or `.WithInertiaPrecognition()` and `AddValidation()`. Endpoint construction throws when validation resolvers are missing. Routing can construct endpoints lazily. See [Validation](/docs/validation-and-errors).

## 419 in tests

1. Use a cookie-preserving client.
2. Load an Inertia page first.
3. Use `request.WithXsrfToken(pageResponse)` on the form request.

See [Testing](/docs/testing#testing-a-form-with-antiforgery).

## Precognition: login locks users out while typing

Precognitive POSTs pass through rate limiting. Use separate bounded partitions for validation and for submission, and validate on blur. See [Precognition](/docs/precognition#rate-limiting). A throttled validation still rejects, so show a retry message. To render a custom Inertia error page for a real submission rejected with 429, add 429 with `AddInertiaErrorPages(o => o.StatusCodes.Add(429))` and put `UseInertiaErrorPages()` before `UseRateLimiter()`. Precognitive JSON responses keep their 429 and `Precognition: true` header.

## 'Location' is a type but is used like a variable

The imported static `Location` name may collide with a type. Call `Inertia.Net.Inertia.Location(url)` explicitly, or opt out with `<InertiaNetImplicitUsings>false</InertiaNetImplicitUsings>` and add your own imports. See [Configuration](/docs/configuration#name-collisions).

## A cached prop loader runs every request

Check that the key and duration are stable and the cache store works. Dot-key props support caching. Include every user or tenant dependency in the cache key. A stale refresh needs its own scope and may be dropped when the background queue is full. See [Props](/docs/props#cached-props).

---

# Build a todo app

URL: https://inertia-dotnet.temtem.dev/docs/forget-me-not

> Build ForgetMeNot step by step with shadcn/ui, covering sign-in, shared lists, infinite scroll, live reminders and server-side rendering, using named routes, typed routes and caching.

ForgetMeNot is a small todo app. It is small, but it uses the same pieces as a real product:

- sign-in
- private data
- a public page
- a long list that loads as you scroll
- a reminder that appears on your screen without a refresh

Each step tells you **what** to do and **why**. If you know why a line is there, you can change it later with confidence.

<Callout type="info" title="What you need">
- The .NET 10 or .NET 11 SDK
- Bun, npm, pnpm or Yarn. The commands on this page use Bun. If you use another tool, use it in place of Bun.
- A code editor and a terminal

You do not need a database server. The app uses SQLite, a database that lives in one file.
</Callout>

## What you will build

Each feature in this table shows one idea from Inertia.Net. The right column names the idea.

| You build | You learn |
|---|---|
| A polished interface | shadcn/ui cards, lists, switches and a theme you can change in one place |
| Sign in with a cookie | The `--auth` starter, redirects to the login page, and a sign-in rate limit |
| A page of lists | Page records, named routes and the typed `routes.ts` file |
| A form that checks itself | Precognition: the server validates a field as you type |
| Slow numbers that load after the page | Deferred props, plus a cache you clear when data changes |
| A list with thousands of items | `ToPageAsync` and infinite scroll |
| A link anyone can open | Server-side rendering and the SSR cache |
| A reminder that shows up by itself | Live props over SignalR |
| Tests | `Inertia.Net.Testing` |

## 1. Create the app

Install the templates once, then create the app. The `--auth` option adds cookie sign-in, so you do not write that yourself. For the other clients, use `--framework vue` or `--framework svelte`. Then pick the matching tab in the examples below.

```sh
dotnet new install Inertia.Net.Templates::1.9.8
dotnet new inertia -n ForgetMeNot --framework react --auth
cd ForgetMeNot
bun install
```

Start the two development processes and keep both terminals open:

```sh
# terminal 1: the frontend (Vite)
bun run dev

# terminal 2: the backend
dotnet watch
```

Open `http://localhost:5180`, click **Log in**, and sign in with `demo@example.com` and the password `password`. Try the pages before you change anything.

<Callout type="info" title="Why two processes?">
Vite serves your React, Vue or Svelte code and reloads it when you save. ASP.NET Core serves the pages. While Vite runs, it writes a small file called `wwwroot/hot`. The app reads this file to find Vite. You do not need to set up anything else.
</Callout>

The template is not empty. It already uses the features this tutorial needs. This table shows where they are:

| Where | What it does | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `HomePage`, `LoginPage` in `Program.cs` | **Page records.** A record that names its component once: `Component => "Home"` | The props and the page name stay together, and the compiler checks them |
| `.WithName("login")` on each route | **Named routes** | The name stays the same when the URL changes. You can change the URL and nothing breaks |
| `ClientApp/types/routes.ts` | **Typed routes**, written from the names | In the browser you write `routes.login()`, never the string `"/login"` |
| `ClientApp/types/inertia.d.ts` | TypeScript types for every page, written from the C# records | A renamed property is a compile error, not a blank spot on the page |
| `.WithInertiaPrecognition()` on the login | The form checks a field on the server when you leave it | One set of rules, run in the browser and on the server |
| `AddInertiaErrorPages()` | A 404 or 500 shows your `Error` page | Visitors never see a raw error |

The app rewrites both generated files, `ClientApp/types/routes.ts` and `ClientApp/types/inertia.d.ts`, when it starts in Development. Never edit them by hand.

## 2. Make it look good with shadcn/ui

The template's pages have almost no styling. This step adds **shadcn/ui**, a set of components: cards, inputs, checkboxes, switches, lists and more. The components are built on Tailwind CSS. They are *copied into your project*, so you own the code and can change any of it.

First, add Tailwind CSS and an `@` shortcut for imports. With the shortcut, you write `@/components/ui/button` instead of `../../components/ui/button`. Start by installing Tailwind CSS:

```sh
bun add -d tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
```

In `vite.config.ts`, add the Tailwind plugin and the alias. Everything else stays as it is:

```ts
import path from 'node:path'
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite'
// ...your other imports

export default defineConfig(({ command }) => ({
  // react(), vue() or svelte() stays where it is; just add tailwindcss() to the list
  plugins: [react(), tailwindcss(), inertia(), hotFile()],
  resolve: { alias: { '@': path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'ClientApp') } },
  // ...the rest stays the same
}))
```

In `tsconfig.json`, add this inside `compilerOptions`, so TypeScript understands the same shortcut:

```json
"paths": { "@/*": ["./ClientApp/*"] }
```

Create `ClientApp/app.css` with one line. Then import it at the top of the client entry file. The client entry file is `ClientApp/app.tsx` for React, and `ClientApp/app.ts` for Vue and Svelte:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
```

```ts
import './app.css'
```

Now run the shadcn setup and add the components this app needs. The flags answer the setup questions in advance. The `nova` preset is a clean neutral look. If you leave the flags out, the tool asks you the questions instead.

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```sh
bunx --bun shadcn@latest init -t vite -b radix -p nova -y --no-monorepo --no-reinstall
bunx --bun shadcn@latest add button card input label badge checkbox alert skeleton switch progress empty item field separator
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```sh
bunx --bun shadcn-vue@latest init -t vite -p nova -y
bunx --bun shadcn-vue@latest add button card input label badge checkbox alert skeleton switch progress empty item field separator
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```sh
bunx --bun shadcn-svelte@latest init --preset nova --base-color neutral --css ClientApp/app.css \
  --components-alias @/components --lib-alias @/lib --utils-alias @/lib/utils \
  --hooks-alias @/hooks --ui-alias @/components/ui
bunx --bun shadcn-svelte@latest add button card input label badge checkbox alert skeleton switch progress empty item field separator
```

The Svelte tool asks before it changes `app.css`. Answer yes.

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Look in `ClientApp/components/ui`. Those files are yours now. Open `button` and you see ordinary code, not a library.

<Callout type="info" title="Why copy components instead of installing a package?">
A library that does almost what you want is hard to change. These components are plain files in your repo. To make a button rounder, edit its file. There is no version to upgrade and nothing hidden. You rarely need to edit a file, though. **Theming**, in the next section, changes the look of every component at once.
</Callout>

### Make the theme yours

Every shadcn component reads a few CSS variables, such as `--primary` for the main color. Add this to the end of `ClientApp/app.css`, and every button, switch and progress bar turns violet with rounder corners:

```css
/* Our theme: a violet primary and rounder corners. Every shadcn component reads these variables. */
:root {
    --primary: oklch(0.51 0.23 277);
    --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);
    --ring: oklch(0.62 0.18 277);
    --radius: 0.75rem;
}

.dark {
    --primary: oklch(0.68 0.19 277);
    --primary-foreground: oklch(0.2 0.02 277);
}
```

Try other values to see how much one line changes. The `.dark` block applies when the root element of the page has the `dark` class. This tutorial does not add a switch for it, but the theme is ready for one.

### The login page

The template's login page is plain HTML, and Tailwind removes the default styles of plain HTML. Replace the login page with a card. A `Field` groups a label, an input and its error message. The error then appears in the right place, and screen readers announce it.

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
// ClientApp/pages/Auth/Login.tsx
import { useForm } from '@inertiajs/react'
import type { FormEvent } from 'react'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
import { Field, FieldError, FieldGroup, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/field'
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
import Layout from '../../Layout'
import type { InertiaPages } from '../../types/inertia'
import { routes } from '../../types/routes'

export default function Login({ returnUrl }: InertiaPages['Auth/Login']) {
  // Precognition: each field is checked on the server when you leave it, with the same rules as the submit.
  const form = useForm({ email: '', password: '', returnUrl }).withPrecognition(routes.login.store())

  const submit = (e: FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    form.submit(routes.login.store(), { onFinish: () => form.reset('password') })
  }

  return (
    <Layout>
      <Card className="mx-auto max-w-sm">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Welcome back</CardTitle>
          <CardDescription>Use demo@example.com and the password "password".</CardDescription>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <form onSubmit={submit}>
            <FieldGroup>
              <Field data-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.email)}>
                <FieldLabel htmlFor="email">Email</FieldLabel>
                <Input
                  id="email"
                  type="email"
                  name="email"
                  autoComplete="username"
                  value={form.data.email}
                  onChange={(e) => form.setData('email', e.target.value)}
                  onBlur={() => form.validate('email')}
                  aria-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.email)}
                />
                <FieldError>{form.errors.email}</FieldError>
              </Field>
              <Field data-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.password)}>
                <FieldLabel htmlFor="password">Password</FieldLabel>
                <Input
                  id="password"
                  type="password"
                  name="password"
                  autoComplete="current-password"
                  value={form.data.password}
                  onChange={(e) => form.setData('password', e.target.value)}
                  onBlur={() => form.validate('password')}
                  aria-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.password)}
                />
                <FieldError>{form.errors.password}</FieldError>
              </Field>
              <Button type="submit" disabled={form.processing}>Log in</Button>
            </FieldGroup>
          </form>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </Layout>
  )
}
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<!-- ClientApp/pages/Auth/Login.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useForm } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
import { Field, FieldError, FieldGroup, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/field'
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
import Layout from '../../Layout.vue'
import type { InertiaPages } from '../../types/inertia'
import { routes } from '../../types/routes'

const props = defineProps<InertiaPages['Auth/Login']>()

// Precognition: each field is checked on the server when you leave it, with the same rules as the submit.
const form = useForm({ email: '', password: '', returnUrl: props.returnUrl }).withPrecognition(routes.login.store())
const submit = () => form.submit(routes.login.store(), { onFinish: () => form.reset('password') })
</script>

<template>
  <Layout>
    <Card class="mx-auto max-w-sm">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Welcome back</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>Use demo@example.com and the password "password".</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <form @submit.prevent="submit">
          <FieldGroup>
            <Field :data-invalid="Boolean(form.errors.email)">
              <FieldLabel for="email">Email</FieldLabel>
              <Input id="email" v-model="form.email" type="email" name="email" autocomplete="username" :aria-invalid="Boolean(form.errors.email)" @blur="form.validate('email')" />
              <FieldError v-if="form.errors.email">{{ form.errors.email }}</FieldError>
            </Field>
            <Field :data-invalid="Boolean(form.errors.password)">
              <FieldLabel for="password">Password</FieldLabel>
              <Input id="password" v-model="form.password" type="password" name="password" autocomplete="current-password" :aria-invalid="Boolean(form.errors.password)" @blur="form.validate('password')" />
              <FieldError v-if="form.errors.password">{{ form.errors.password }}</FieldError>
            </Field>
            <Button type="submit" :disabled="form.processing">Log in</Button>
          </FieldGroup>
        </form>
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  </Layout>
</template>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```svelte
<!-- ClientApp/pages/Auth/Login.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { useForm } from '@inertiajs/svelte'
  import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
  import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
  import { Field, FieldError, FieldGroup, FieldLabel } from '@/components/ui/field'
  import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
  import Layout from '../../Layout.svelte'
  import type { InertiaPages } from '../../types/inertia'
  import { routes } from '../../types/routes'

  let { returnUrl }: InertiaPages['Auth/Login'] = $props()

  // Precognition: each field is checked on the server when you leave it, with the same rules as the submit.
  const form = useForm({ email: '', password: '', returnUrl }).withPrecognition(routes.login.store())
  const submit = (e: SubmitEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    form.submit(routes.login.store(), { onFinish: () => form.reset('password') })
  }
</script>

<Layout>
  <Card class="mx-auto max-w-sm">
    <CardHeader>
      <CardTitle>Welcome back</CardTitle>
      <CardDescription>Use demo@example.com and the password "password".</CardDescription>
    </CardHeader>

      <form onsubmit={submit}>
        <FieldGroup>
          <Field data-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.email)}>
            <FieldLabel for="email">Email</FieldLabel>
            <Input id="email" type="email" name="email" autocomplete="username" bind:value={form.email} onblur={() => form.validate('email')} aria-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.email)} />
            {#if form.errors.email}<FieldError>{form.errors.email}</FieldError>{/if}
          </Field>
          <Field data-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.password)}>
            <FieldLabel for="password">Password</FieldLabel>
            <Input id="password" type="password" name="password" autocomplete="current-password" bind:value={form.password} onblur={() => form.validate('password')} aria-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.password)} />
            {#if form.errors.password}<FieldError>{form.errors.password}</FieldError>{/if}
          </Field>
          <Button type="submit" disabled={form.processing}>Log in</Button>
        </FieldGroup>
      </form>
    </CardContent>
  </Card>
</Layout>
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The form still uses `withPrecognition`. When you leave a field, the server checks that field with the same rules as the real submit. Open `http://localhost:5180/login` to see the new look.

## 3. Add a database

Lists and items must survive a restart, so the app needs a database. This tutorial uses **EF Core with SQLite**. EF Core is the usual way to use a database from C#, and SQLite needs no server. Install the two packages:

```sh
dotnet add package Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite --version "10.*"
dotnet add package Inertia.Net.EntityFrameworkCore --version 1.9.8
```

<Callout type="tip" title="On .NET 11?">
Use `--version "11.*"` for the SQLite package. The EF Core version must match your .NET version.
</Callout>

Create `Data.cs`. Its classes are the **database shape**. They are not what the browser sees. Step 4 covers that.

```csharp
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

namespace ForgetMeNot;

public sealed class TodoList
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public required string OwnerEmail { get; set; }
    public required string Title { get; set; }

    /// <summary>The secret part of the public URL. Null while the list is private.</summary>
    public string? ShareSlug { get; set; }

    public List<TodoItem> Items { get; } = [];
}

public sealed class TodoItem
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public int TodoListId { get; set; }
    public TodoList List { get; set; } = null!;
    public required string Title { get; set; }
    public bool IsDone { get; set; }

    // / <summary>When to remind the owner, in UTC. Null means no reminder. (A DateTime, not a
    // DateTimeOffset: SQLite cannot compare those in a query.)</summary>
    public DateTime? RemindAt { get; set; }

    /// <summary>Set once the reminder has fired, so a restart never sends it twice.</summary>
    public DateTime? RemindedAt { get; set; }
}

public sealed class AppDb(DbContextOptions<AppDb> options) : DbContext(options)
{
    public DbSet<TodoList> Lists => Set<TodoList>();
    public DbSet<TodoItem> Items => Set<TodoItem>();

    protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder model)
    {
        model.Entity<TodoList>().HasIndex(l => l.OwnerEmail);
        model.Entity<TodoList>().HasIndex(l => l.ShareSlug).IsUnique();
    }
}
```

A few choices are worth explaining:

- **`OwnerEmail` instead of a users table.** The template's demo user already has an email in the sign-in cookie. Using that email as the owner key keeps this guide short. In a real app you would use ASP.NET Core Identity and a user id.
- **`ShareSlug` is null until you share.** A random secret in the URL is the only thing that opens a public list. There is nothing to guess. When you turn sharing off, the app removes the secret.
- **`RemindedAt` makes reminders safe to repeat.** If the app restarts halfway through, a reminder that was already sent is never sent twice.
- **`DateTime`, not `DateTimeOffset`, for reminders.** SQLite cannot compare `DateTimeOffset` values inside a query. The app stores UTC times as plain `DateTime`, so the query `RemindAt <= now` works.

Now open `Program.cs`. First, **delete the demo todo code** that came with the template. Your own code replaces it. Delete these parts:

- the `AddSingleton<TodoStore>()` line
- the `/todos` endpoints (the ones named `todos.index`, `todos.store`, `todos.toggle` and `todos.destroy`)
- the `/dashboard` endpoint and the `DashboardPage` record
- the `Todo`, `TodoStats`, `TodosPage`, `NewTodo` and `TodoStore` types
- their lines in `AppJsonContext` at the bottom

Then register the database in `Program.cs`, where the other services are registered:

```csharp
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore; // at the top of the file

builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDb>(o =>
    o.UseSqlite(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Default") ?? "Data Source=forgetmenot.db"));
```

Then create the tables right after `var app = builder.Build();`:

```csharp
using (var scope = app.Services.CreateScope())
{
    // fine for a first app; use migrations later
    scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<AppDb>().Database.EnsureCreated();
}
```

<Callout type="info" title="Why read the connection string from configuration?">
Production and tests need a different database than your laptop. With `GetConnectionString("Default")`, they can set `ConnectionStrings:Default` without a code change. The tests in this tutorial use this.
</Callout>

`EnsureCreated()` builds the tables on the first run. It cannot change them later. When the model changes in a real app, switch to EF Core migrations.

## 4. Decide what the browser sees

Never send a database entity to the browser. An entity may have columns you did not mean to share, such as `OwnerEmail`. Every change to the table would also change your page. Instead, send small **records** that hold only what a page needs.

Create `Models.cs`:

```csharp
using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
using System.Security.Claims;

namespace ForgetMeNot;

// What the browser receives: small records, never the database entities.

public sealed record ListCard(int Id, string Title, int Open, int Total, bool IsShared);
public sealed record Stats(int Open, int Done);
public sealed record ReminderRow(int Id, int ListId, string Title, DateTime RemindAt);
public sealed record ListHeader(int Id, string Title, bool IsShared, string? ShareUrl);
public sealed record ItemRow(int Id, string Title, bool IsDone, DateTime? RemindAt);
public sealed record PublicHeader(string Title, int Open);
public sealed record PublicItem(int Id, string Title);

// What the browser sends. These are public classes because the AddValidation() generator skips internal
// types.

public sealed class NewList
{
    [Required, StringLength(80)]
    public string? Title { get; set; }
}

public sealed class NewItem
{
    [Required, StringLength(200)]
    public string? Title { get; set; }

    public DateTime? RemindAt { get; set; }
}

// / <summary>An event name plus the channel it travels on. The page and the publisher both use this one
// value.</summary>
public static class Events
{
    public static LiveEvent RemindersChanged(string email) => new("RemindersChanged", LiveChannel.Private($"users.{email}"));
}

public static class UserExtensions
{
    /// <summary>The signed-in person's email: our key for "whose list is this?".</summary>
    public static string Email(this ClaimsPrincipal user) => user.FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.Email)!;
}
```

Three things here are easy to miss:

- **Form classes are `public`.** The validation generator, `AddValidation()`, skips `internal` types. With a private form class, the `[Required]` rules do nothing, and you get no error.
- **`Events.RemindersChanged(email)` is one value used twice.** The page uses it to say "refresh me when this happens", and the worker uses it to say "this happened". Because both use the same value, the page and the worker always agree.
- **`Email()` hides one claim lookup.** Every endpoint asks the same question, "whose list is this?", so the code asks it in one place.

The template turned off reflection-based JSON. This keeps the app ready for Native AOT. In return, you must list every type that goes to or from the browser. Add these lines to `AppJsonContext` at the bottom of `Program.cs`:

```csharp
[JsonSerializable(typeof(ListCard))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Stats))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(List<ReminderRow>))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Page<ItemRow>))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(Page<PublicItem>))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(NewList))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(NewItem))]
```

Each page record gets its own line when you create it: `ListsPage` in step 5, `ListPage` in step 6 and `PublicPage` in step 7.

<Callout type="tip" title="Forgot one?">
If you forget a type, you get an error the first time the app sends that type. The message names the type. Add the type to `AppJsonContext` and try again.
</Callout>

## 5. The lists page

A **page record** holds the props of a page, which are the values the server sends to the page component. It also holds the code that fills them. Create `ListsPage.cs`:

```csharp
using System.Security.Claims;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

namespace ForgetMeNot;

public sealed record ListsPage(
    List<ListCard> Lists,
    [property: InertiaPropType(typeof(Stats))] InertiaProp Stats,
    [property: InertiaPropType(typeof(List<ReminderRow>))] InertiaProp Reminders) : IInertiaPage
{
    public static string Component => "Lists/Index";

    public static async Task<IResult> Handle(ClaimsPrincipal user, AppDb db, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var email = user.Email();

        var lists = await db.Lists.AsNoTracking()
            .Where(l => l.OwnerEmail == email)
            .OrderBy(l => l.Title)
            .Select(l => new ListCard(l.Id, l.Title, l.Items.Count(i => !i.IsDone), l.Items.Count, l.ShareSlug != null))
            .ToListAsync(ct);

        return Render(new ListsPage(
            lists,
            // Slow part: sent after the page shows. Cached per person, and cleared by tag whenever their
            // data changes.
            Defer(c => LoadStats(db, email, c))
                .Cache($"stats:{email}", TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5), tags: [$"user:{email}"]),
            // Refreshes by itself when the reminder worker publishes this event.
            Defer(c => LoadReminders(db, email, c)).Live(Events.RemindersChanged(email))));
    }

    private static async Task<Stats> LoadStats(AppDb db, string email, CancellationToken ct) =>
        new(await db.Items.CountAsync(i => i.List.OwnerEmail == email && !i.IsDone, ct),
            await db.Items.CountAsync(i => i.List.OwnerEmail == email && i.IsDone, ct));

    private static Task<List<ReminderRow>> LoadReminders(AppDb db, string email, CancellationToken ct) =>
        db.Items.AsNoTracking()
            .Where(i => i.List.OwnerEmail == email && i.RemindedAt != null && !i.IsDone)
            .OrderByDescending(i => i.Id)
            .Take(10)
            .Select(i => new ReminderRow(i.Id, i.TodoListId, i.Title, i.RemindAt!.Value))
            .ToListAsync(ct);
}
```

Add `[JsonSerializable(typeof(ListsPage))]` to `AppJsonContext`, then read the handler from top to bottom:

1. The query reads `lists` straight from the database into `ListCard` records. `AsNoTracking()` tells EF Core that the code will not change these rows, which makes the query cheaper.
2. `Stats` is **deferred**. The server sends the page right away, and the browser asks for the numbers a moment later. The visitor sees the page sooner, even if counting is slow.
3. `.Cache(...)` keeps the finished stats for five minutes, so a second visit does not count again. The `tags` give you a way to clear the cached stats. Every write removes the tag `user:email`, so the numbers are never wrong for long.
4. `Reminders` is deferred and **live**. Step 8 explains it.

Now add the routes. Create `Endpoints.cs`:

```csharp
using System.Security.Claims;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

namespace ForgetMeNot;

public static class ForgetMeNotEndpoints
{
    public static void MapForgetMeNot(this IEndpointRouteBuilder app)
    {
        // Everything in this group needs a signed-in person. The cookie handler sends everyone else to
        // /login.
        var signedIn = app.MapGroup("").RequireAuthorization();

        // Each .WithName(...) gives the route a typed function in ClientApp/types/routes.ts.
        signedIn.MapGet("/lists", ListsPage.Handle).WithName("lists.index");

        signedIn.MapPost("/lists", async (
            NewList input, ClaimsPrincipal user, AppDb db, IInertiaCache cache, CancellationToken ct) =>
        {
            var list = new TodoList { OwnerEmail = user.Email(), Title = input.Title!.Trim() };
            db.Lists.Add(list);
            await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
            // the cached stats are out of date now
            await cache.RemoveByTagAsync($"user:{user.Email()}", ct);
            return Results.Redirect($"/lists/{list.Id}");
        }).WithInertiaPrecognition().WithName("lists.store");
    }
}
```

Call the new method from `Program.cs`, in the place where the `/dashboard` endpoint was:

```csharp
app.MapForgetMeNot(); // our lists, items and the public page
```

Also send people to their lists after they sign in. In the `/login` endpoint, change the last `"/dashboard"` to `"/lists"`.

<Callout type="info" title="Why these routes have names">
`.WithName("lists.store")` costs nothing and gives you two things. First, the name becomes `routes.lists.store()` in your frontend, so you never type `"/lists"` again. Second, the form's type, `RouteBodies['lists.store']`, comes from the C# class `NewList`, so the C# and the TypeScript cannot disagree.
</Callout>

<Callout type="info" title="Why .WithInertiaPrecognition()?">
`.WithInertiaPrecognition()` does two jobs. First, it sends a normal submit with bad data back to the form with the error messages. Second, the page can ask "is this one field valid?" while the person is still typing, and the server answers without running your code. You write the rules once, on the class, with `[Required]` and `[StringLength]`.
</Callout>

### Make the frontend ready

Write the types file and the routes file now. The app does this by itself when it starts in Development. This command does it when you ask, which is useful in CI:

```sh
bun run types
```

Open `ClientApp/types/routes.ts`. It contains functions you did not write, one for each named route:

```ts
routes.lists.index()            // { url: '/lists', method: 'get' }
routes.lists.store()            // { url: '/lists', method: 'post' }
routes.lists.index.url()        // '/lists'
```

Now run the build, which also checks the types. It should fail, and that is expected:

```sh
bun run build
```

You deleted the `todos` and `dashboard` routes, so TypeScript lists every place that still uses them: the layout and the home page. A URL written as a string would fail without an error, in front of a visitor. A typed route fails during development, where you see it.

Fix them one by one. Start with the layout, which every page uses. It has the top bar with the **My lists** link and the **Log out** button. It also has an `Alert` for the **flash** messages, which are the messages the server sends after an action:

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
// ClientApp/Layout.tsx
import { Link, router, usePage } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { CircleAlert, CircleCheck, ListChecks, LogOut } from 'lucide-react'
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Alert, AlertDescription } from '@/components/ui/alert'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { routes } from './types/routes'

export default function Layout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  // props.appName, props.auth and flash are typed by types/inertia.d.ts.
  const { props, flash } = usePage()
  const user = props.auth.user

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen bg-muted/30">
      <header className="border-b bg-background">
        <div className="mx-auto flex h-14 max-w-3xl items-center gap-2 px-4">
          <Link href={routes.home()} className="mr-2 flex items-center gap-2 font-semibold">
            <ListChecks className="size-5 text-primary" />
            {props.appName}
          </Link>
          {user ? (
            <>
              <Button asChild variant="ghost" size="sm">
                <Link href={routes.lists.index()}>My lists</Link>
              </Button>
              <span className="ml-auto hidden text-sm text-muted-foreground sm:inline">{user.name}</span>
              <Button variant="outline" size="sm" className="ml-auto sm:ml-0" onClick={() => router.visit(routes.logout())}>
                <LogOut /> Log out
              </Button>
            </>
          ) : (
            <Button asChild size="sm" className="ml-auto">
              <Link href={routes.login()}>Log in</Link>
            </Button>
          )}
        </div>
      </header>

      <main className="mx-auto max-w-3xl space-y-6 px-4 py-8">
        {flash.success && (
          <Alert>
            <CircleCheck />
            <AlertDescription>{flash.success}</AlertDescription>
          </Alert>
        )}
        {flash.error && (
          <Alert variant="destructive">
            <CircleAlert />
            <AlertDescription>{flash.error}</AlertDescription>
          </Alert>
        )}
        {children}
      </main>
    </div>
  )
}
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<!-- ClientApp/Layout.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Link, router, usePage } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
import { CircleAlert, CircleCheck, ListChecks, LogOut } from '@lucide/vue'
import { computed } from 'vue'
import { Alert, AlertDescription } from '@/components/ui/alert'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { routes } from './types/routes'

// page.props.appName, page.props.auth and page.flash are typed by types/inertia.d.ts.
const page = usePage()
const user = computed(() => page.props.auth.user)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="min-h-screen bg-muted/30">
    <header class="border-b bg-background">
      <div class="mx-auto flex h-14 max-w-3xl items-center gap-2 px-4">
        <Link :href="routes.home()" class="mr-2 flex items-center gap-2 font-semibold">
          <ListChecks class="size-5 text-primary" />
          {{ page.props.appName }}
        </Link>
        <template v-if="user">
          <Button as-child variant="ghost" size="sm">
            <Link :href="routes.lists.index()">My lists</Link>
          </Button>
          <span class="ml-auto hidden text-sm text-muted-foreground sm:inline">{{ user.name }}</span>
          <Button variant="outline" size="sm" class="ml-auto sm:ml-0" @click="router.visit(routes.logout())">
            <LogOut /> Log out
          </Button>
        </template>
        <Button v-else as-child size="sm" class="ml-auto">
          <Link :href="routes.login()">Log in</Link>
        </Button>
      </div>
    </header>

    <main class="mx-auto max-w-3xl space-y-6 px-4 py-8">
      <Alert v-if="page.flash.success">
        <CircleCheck />
        <AlertDescription>{{ page.flash.success }}</AlertDescription>
      </Alert>
      <Alert v-if="page.flash.error" variant="destructive">
        <CircleAlert />
        <AlertDescription>{{ page.flash.error }}</AlertDescription>
      </Alert>
      <slot />
    </main>
  </div>
</template>
```

  </Tab>
