Finally delete `ClientApp/pages/Todos` and the Dashboard page (`Dashboard.tsx`, `Dashboard.vue` or `Dashboard.svelte`). Run `bun run build` again. It passes.

<Callout type="info" title="Why a warning appears when you build the C#">
`dotnet build` prints `INERTIA002` for `ListsPage`: "this component has no file under `ClientApp/pages`". The warning exists to catch a typo, or a page you forgot to write. It goes away in the next step, when you add the page.
</Callout>

## 6. One list, with infinite scroll

A list can have thousands of items. Sending them all would make the page slow. Instead, the server sends one page of items. The browser asks for the next page when the reader scrolls to the end.

Create `ListPage.cs`, and add `[JsonSerializable(typeof(ListPage))]` to `AppJsonContext`:

```csharp
using System.Security.Claims;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

namespace ForgetMeNot;

public sealed record ListPage(
    ListHeader List,
    [property: InertiaPropType(typeof(Page<ItemRow>))] InertiaProp Items) : IInertiaPage
{
    public static string Component => "Lists/Show";

    public static async Task<IResult> Handle(
        int id, PageRequest request, ClaimsPrincipal user, AppDb db, LinkGenerator links, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var email = user.Email();

        var row = await db.Lists.AsNoTracking()
            // another person's list looks like a missing one
            .Where(l => l.Id == id && l.OwnerEmail == email)
            .Select(l => new { l.Id, l.Title, l.ShareSlug })
            .FirstOrDefaultAsync(ct);
        if (row is null) return Results.NotFound();

        // Named routes work on the server too: ask the link generator for the public address of this list.
        var shareUrl = row.ShareSlug is null ? null : links.GetPathByName("public.show", new { slug = row.ShareSlug });
        var list = new ListHeader(row.Id, row.Title, row.ShareSlug is not null, shareUrl);

        // ToPageAsync adds Skip/Take and counts the rows. A unique order (Id last) keeps pages from
        // overlapping.
        var items = await db.Items.AsNoTracking()
            .Where(i => i.TodoListId == id)
            .OrderBy(i => i.IsDone).ThenBy(i => i.Id)
            .Select(i => new ItemRow(i.Id, i.Title, i.IsDone, i.RemindAt))
            .ToPageAsync(request, ct: ct);

        return Render(new ListPage(list, Scroll(items)));
    }
}
```

- **`.ToPageAsync(request)`** comes from `Inertia.Net.EntityFrameworkCore`. It adds `Skip` and `Take` for you and counts the rows. `PageRequest` reads `?page=2` from the URL by itself.
- **The order must be unique.** The query sorts by `IsDone` and then by `Id`. If two items could tie, a row might appear on two pages or on none.
- **`Scroll(items)`** tells the browser that this value is a list that grows. New pages are merged into `items.data` instead of replacing it.
- **Someone else's list is a 404.** The query asks for the id and the owner together. The response does not reveal that the list exists.
- **`links.GetPathByName("public.show", ...)`** is a named route used on the **server**. The page needs the public address, and the name builds it, so the URL pattern is written in one place only. You add the route in step 7. Until then, the address is empty.

Add the rest of the routes to `Endpoints.cs`, inside `MapForgetMeNot`, after the two list routes. Also add `using System.Security.Cryptography;` at the top of the file:

```csharp
signedIn.MapGet("/lists/{id:int}", ListPage.Handle).WithName("lists.show");

signedIn.MapPost("/lists/{id:int}/items", async (
    int id, NewItem input, ClaimsPrincipal user, AppDb db, IInertiaCache cache, CancellationToken ct) =>
{
    if (!await db.Lists.AnyAsync(l => l.Id == id && l.OwnerEmail == user.Email(), ct)) return Results.NotFound();

    db.Items.Add(new TodoItem { TodoListId = id, Title = input.Title!.Trim(), RemindAt = input.RemindAt });
    await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
    await cache.RemoveByTagAsync($"user:{user.Email()}", ct);
    return Back($"/lists/{id}").WithFlash("success", "Added");
}).WithInertiaPrecognition().WithName("items.store");

signedIn.MapPatch("/items/{id:int}/toggle", async (
    int id, ClaimsPrincipal user, AppDb db, IInertiaCache cache, CancellationToken ct) =>
{
    var item = await db.Items.FirstOrDefaultAsync(i => i.Id == id && i.List.OwnerEmail == user.Email(), ct);
    if (item is null) return Results.NotFound();

    item.IsDone = !item.IsDone;
    await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
    await cache.RemoveByTagAsync($"user:{user.Email()}", ct);
    return Back($"/lists/{item.TodoListId}");
}).WithName("items.toggle");

signedIn.MapDelete("/items/{id:int}", async (
    int id, ClaimsPrincipal user, AppDb db, IInertiaCache cache, CancellationToken ct) =>
{
    var item = await db.Items.FirstOrDefaultAsync(i => i.Id == id && i.List.OwnerEmail == user.Email(), ct);
    if (item is null) return Results.NotFound();

    db.Items.Remove(item);
    await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
    await cache.RemoveByTagAsync($"user:{user.Email()}", ct);
    return Back($"/lists/{item.TodoListId}").WithFlash("success", "Deleted");
}).WithName("items.destroy");

// Turn sharing on (make a secret link) or off (forget it, so the old link stops working).
signedIn.MapPost("/lists/{id:int}/share", async (
    int id, ClaimsPrincipal user, AppDb db, CancellationToken ct) =>
{
    var list = await db.Lists.FirstOrDefaultAsync(l => l.Id == id && l.OwnerEmail == user.Email(), ct);
    if (list is null) return Results.NotFound();

    list.ShareSlug = list.ShareSlug is null ? Convert.ToHexString(RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(8)).ToLowerInvariant() : null;
    await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
    return Back($"/lists/{id}");
}).WithName("lists.share");
```

Notice the pattern. Each write does the same things in the same order:

1. It **checks the owner in the query**.
2. It **saves**.
3. It **clears the stats cache**.
4. It **sends the person back** with `Back(...)`.

`Back` returns the person to the page they came from, so the page shows the new state. `WithFlash` carries the one-time message.

<Callout type="warning" title="Do not forget the owner check">
`GET /lists/5` is protected, but `PATCH /items/9` is a separate endpoint and needs its own check. Every endpoint that takes an id must check that the id belongs to the signed-in person. A missing owner check is the most common security bug in apps like this one.
</Callout>

Sharing works like this. The first press of the share button creates a random secret. The second press removes it. Eight random bytes are 16 characters that nobody can guess. Do not use `Random` or a counter for a secret.

Run `bun run types` again, so the browser knows the new routes and pages. Then add the two pages.

First, the lists page. `useForm` holds the form's values. `withPrecognition` adds `validate` to the form, and `validate` asks the server about one field:

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
// ClientApp/pages/Lists/Index.tsx
import { Deferred, Link, useForm } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { BellRing, ChevronRight, CircleCheck, ListTodo, Plus } from 'lucide-react'
import type { FormEvent } from 'react'
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
import { Empty, EmptyDescription, EmptyHeader, EmptyMedia, EmptyTitle } from '@/components/ui/empty'
import { Field, FieldError } from '@/components/ui/field'
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
import { Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemMedia, ItemTitle } from '@/components/ui/item'
import { Progress } from '@/components/ui/progress'
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/skeleton'
import Layout from '../../Layout'
import type { InertiaPages } from '../../types/inertia'
import { routes, type RouteBodies } from '../../types/routes'

export default function Index({ lists, stats, reminders }: InertiaPages['Lists/Index']) {
  // The form's fields come from the C# NewList class, and withPrecognition checks the title on the server as you type.
  const form = useForm<RouteBodies['lists.store']>({ title: '' }).withPrecognition(routes.lists.store())

  const submit = (e: FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    form.submit(routes.lists.store())
  }

  return (
    <Layout>
      <div>
        <h1 className="text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight">My lists</h1>
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Private by default. Share a list when you want to.</p>
      </div>

      {/* Deferred needs a fallback to show while the data loads. */}
      <Deferred
        data="stats"
        fallback={
          <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
            <Skeleton className="h-24" />
            <Skeleton className="h-24" />
          </div>
        }
      >
        <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
          <Card>
            <CardHeader>
              <CardDescription className="flex items-center gap-2"><ListTodo className="size-4" /> Open</CardDescription>
              <CardTitle className="text-3xl tabular-nums">{stats?.open}</CardTitle>
            </CardHeader>
          </Card>
          <Card>
            <CardHeader>
              <CardDescription className="flex items-center gap-2"><CircleCheck className="size-4" /> Done</CardDescription>
              <CardTitle className="text-3xl tabular-nums">{stats?.done}</CardTitle>
            </CardHeader>
          </Card>
        </div>
      </Deferred>

      <Deferred data="reminders" fallback={<></>}>
        {reminders && reminders.length > 0 && (
          <Card className="border-primary/30 bg-primary/5">
            <CardHeader>
              <CardTitle className="flex items-center gap-2"><BellRing className="size-4 text-primary" /> Reminders</CardTitle>
            </CardHeader>
            <CardContent>
              <ItemGroup>
                {reminders.map((r) => (
                  <Item key={r.id} asChild size="sm">
                    <Link href={routes.lists.show(r.listId)}>
                      <ItemContent><ItemTitle>{r.title}</ItemTitle></ItemContent>
                      <ItemActions><Badge>due</Badge></ItemActions>
                    </Link>
                  </Item>
                ))}
              </ItemGroup>
            </CardContent>
          </Card>
        )}
      </Deferred>

      <Card>
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>New list</CardTitle>
          <CardDescription>Give it a short name, like Groceries.</CardDescription>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <form onSubmit={submit} className="space-y-2">
            <div className="flex gap-2">
              <Input
                value={form.data.title ?? ''}
                onChange={(e) => form.setData('title', e.target.value)}
                onBlur={() => form.validate('title')}
                placeholder="A new list"
                aria-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.title)}
              />
              <Button disabled={form.processing}><Plus /> Add</Button>
            </div>
            <Field data-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.title)}>
              <FieldError>{form.errors.title}</FieldError>
            </Field>
          </form>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>

      {lists.length === 0 ? (
        <Empty className="border border-dashed">
          <EmptyHeader>
            <EmptyMedia variant="icon"><ListTodo /></EmptyMedia>
            <EmptyTitle>No lists yet</EmptyTitle>
            <EmptyDescription>Add your first one above.</EmptyDescription>
          </EmptyHeader>
        </Empty>
      ) : (
        <ItemGroup className="gap-3">
          {lists.map((list) => (
            <Item key={list.id} variant="outline" asChild className="bg-card hover:bg-accent/50">
              <Link href={routes.lists.show(list.id)}>
                <ItemContent>
                  <ItemTitle>
                    {list.title}
                    {list.isShared && <Badge variant="secondary">shared</Badge>}
                  </ItemTitle>
                  <ItemDescription>{list.open} open of {list.total}</ItemDescription>
                  <Progress value={list.total === 0 ? 0 : ((list.total - list.open) / list.total) * 100} className="mt-2 h-1.5" />
                </ItemContent>
                <ItemActions><ChevronRight className="size-4 text-muted-foreground" /></ItemActions>
              </Link>
            </Item>
          ))}
        </ItemGroup>
      )}
    </Layout>
  )
}
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue
<!-- ClientApp/pages/Lists/Index.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Deferred, Link, useForm } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
import { BellRing, ChevronRight, CircleCheck, ListTodo, Plus } from '@lucide/vue'
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
import { Empty, EmptyDescription, EmptyHeader, EmptyMedia, EmptyTitle } from '@/components/ui/empty'
import { FieldError } from '@/components/ui/field'
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
import { Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemTitle } from '@/components/ui/item'
import { Progress } from '@/components/ui/progress'
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/skeleton'
import Layout from '../../Layout.vue'
import type { InertiaPages } from '../../types/inertia'
import { routes, type RouteBodies } from '../../types/routes'

defineProps<InertiaPages['Lists/Index']>()

// The form's fields come from the C# NewList class, and withPrecognition checks the title on the server as you type.
const form = useForm<RouteBodies['lists.store']>({ title: '' }).withPrecognition(routes.lists.store())
const submit = () => form.submit(routes.lists.store())
</script>

<template>
  <Layout>
    <div>
      <h1 class="text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight">My lists</h1>
      <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Private by default. Share a list when you want to.</p>
    </div>

    <!-- Deferred needs a fallback to show while the data loads. -->
    <Deferred data="stats">
      <template #fallback>
        <div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
          <Skeleton class="h-24" />
          <Skeleton class="h-24" />
        </div>
      </template>
      <div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
        <Card>
          <CardHeader>
            <CardDescription class="flex items-center gap-2"><ListTodo class="size-4" /> Open</CardDescription>
            <CardTitle class="text-3xl tabular-nums">{{ stats?.open }}</CardTitle>
          </CardHeader>
        </Card>
        <Card>
          <CardHeader>
            <CardDescription class="flex items-center gap-2"><CircleCheck class="size-4" /> Done</CardDescription>
            <CardTitle class="text-3xl tabular-nums">{{ stats?.done }}</CardTitle>
          </CardHeader>
        </Card>
      </div>
    </Deferred>

    <Deferred data="reminders">
      <template #fallback />
      <Card v-if="reminders && reminders.length > 0" class="border-primary/30 bg-primary/5">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle class="flex items-center gap-2"><BellRing class="size-4 text-primary" /> Reminders</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <ItemGroup>
            <Item v-for="r in reminders" :key="r.id" as-child size="sm">
              <Link :href="routes.lists.show(r.listId)">
                <ItemContent><ItemTitle>{{ r.title }}</ItemTitle></ItemContent>
                <ItemActions><Badge>due</Badge></ItemActions>
              </Link>
            </Item>
          </ItemGroup>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </Deferred>

    <Card>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>New list</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>Give it a short name, like Groceries.</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <form class="space-y-2" @submit.prevent="submit">
          <div class="flex gap-2">
            <Input :model-value="form.title ?? ''" @update:model-value="form.title = String($event)" placeholder="A new list" :aria-invalid="Boolean(form.errors.title)" @blur="form.validate('title')" />
            <Button :disabled="form.processing"><Plus /> Add</Button>
          </div>
          <FieldError v-if="form.errors.title">{{ form.errors.title }}</FieldError>
        </form>
      </CardContent>
    </Card>

    <Empty v-if="lists.length === 0" class="border border-dashed">
      <EmptyHeader>
        <EmptyMedia variant="icon"><ListTodo /></EmptyMedia>
        <EmptyTitle>No lists yet</EmptyTitle>
        <EmptyDescription>Add your first one above.</EmptyDescription>
      </EmptyHeader>
    </Empty>
    <ItemGroup v-else class="gap-3">
      <Item v-for="list in lists" :key="list.id" variant="outline" as-child class="bg-card hover:bg-accent/50">
        <Link :href="routes.lists.show(list.id)">
          <ItemContent>
            <ItemTitle>
              {{ list.title }}
              <Badge v-if="list.isShared" variant="secondary">shared</Badge>
            </ItemTitle>
            <ItemDescription>{{ list.open }} open of {{ list.total }}</ItemDescription>
            <Progress :model-value="list.total === 0 ? 0 : ((list.total - list.open) / list.total) * 100" class="mt-2 h-1.5" />
          </ItemContent>
          <ItemActions><ChevronRight class="size-4 text-muted-foreground" /></ItemActions>
        </Link>
      </Item>
    </ItemGroup>
  </Layout>
</template>
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Svelte">

```svelte
<!-- ClientApp/pages/Lists/Index.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { BellRing, ChevronRight, CircleCheck, ListTodo, Plus } from '@lucide/svelte'
  import { Deferred, Link, useForm } from '@inertiajs/svelte'
  import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
  import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
  import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
  import { Empty, EmptyDescription, EmptyHeader, EmptyMedia, EmptyTitle } from '@/components/ui/empty'
  import { FieldError } from '@/components/ui/field'
  import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
  import { Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemTitle } from '@/components/ui/item'
  import { Progress } from '@/components/ui/progress'
  import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/skeleton'
  import Layout from '../../Layout.svelte'
  import type { InertiaPages } from '../../types/inertia'
  import { routes, type RouteBodies } from '../../types/routes'

  let { lists, stats, reminders }: InertiaPages['Lists/Index'] = $props()

  // The form's fields come from the C# NewList class, and withPrecognition checks the title on the server as you type.
  const form = useForm<RouteBodies['lists.store']>({ title: '' }).withPrecognition(routes.lists.store())
  const submit = (e: SubmitEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    form.submit(routes.lists.store())
  }
</script>

<Layout>
  <div>
    <h1 class="text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight">My lists</h1>
    <p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Private by default. Share a list when you want to.</p>
  </div>

  <!-- Deferred needs a fallback to show while the data loads. -->
  <Deferred data="stats">
    {#snippet fallback()}
      <div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
        <Skeleton class="h-24" />
        <Skeleton class="h-24" />
      </div>
    {/snippet}
    <div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
      <Card>
        <CardHeader>
          <CardDescription class="flex items-center gap-2"><ListTodo class="size-4" /> Open</CardDescription>
          <CardTitle class="text-3xl tabular-nums">{stats?.open}</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
      </Card>
      <Card>
        <CardHeader>
          <CardDescription class="flex items-center gap-2"><CircleCheck class="size-4" /> Done</CardDescription>
          <CardTitle class="text-3xl tabular-nums">{stats?.done}</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
      </Card>
    </div>
  </Deferred>

  <Deferred data="reminders">
    {#snippet fallback()}{/snippet}
    {#if reminders && reminders.length > 0}
      <Card class="border-primary/30 bg-primary/5">
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle class="flex items-center gap-2"><BellRing class="size-4 text-primary" /> Reminders</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <ItemGroup>
            {#each reminders as r (r.id)}
              <Item size="sm">
                {#snippet child({ props })}
                  <Link {...props} href={routes.lists.show(r.listId)}>
                    <ItemContent><ItemTitle>{r.title}</ItemTitle></ItemContent>
                    <ItemActions><Badge>due</Badge></ItemActions>
                  </Link>
                {/snippet}
              </Item>
            {/each}
          </ItemGroup>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    {/if}
  </Deferred>

  <Card>
    <CardHeader>
      <CardTitle>New list</CardTitle>
      <CardDescription>Give it a short name, like Groceries.</CardDescription>
    </CardHeader>
    <CardContent>
      <form onsubmit={submit} class="space-y-2">
        <div class="flex gap-2">
          <Input bind:value={form.title} onblur={() => form.validate('title')} placeholder="A new list" aria-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.title)} />
          <Button type="submit" disabled={form.processing}><Plus /> Add</Button>
        </div>
        {#if form.errors.title}<FieldError>{form.errors.title}</FieldError>{/if}
      </form>
    </CardContent>
  </Card>

  {#if lists.length === 0}
    <Empty class="border border-dashed">
      <EmptyHeader>
        <EmptyMedia variant="icon"><ListTodo /></EmptyMedia>
        <EmptyTitle>No lists yet</EmptyTitle>
        <EmptyDescription>Add your first one above.</EmptyDescription>
      </EmptyHeader>
    </Empty>
  {:else}
    <ItemGroup class="gap-3">
      {#each lists as list (list.id)}
        <Item variant="outline" class="bg-card hover:bg-accent/50">
          {#snippet child({ props })}
            <Link {...props} href={routes.lists.show(list.id)}>
              <ItemContent>
                <ItemTitle>
                  {list.title}
                  {#if list.isShared}<Badge variant="secondary">shared</Badge>{/if}
                </ItemTitle>
                <ItemDescription>{list.open} open of {list.total}</ItemDescription>
                <Progress value={list.total === 0 ? 0 : ((list.total - list.open) / list.total) * 100} class="mt-2 h-1.5" />
              </ItemContent>
              <ItemActions><ChevronRight class="size-4 text-muted-foreground" /></ItemActions>
            </Link>
          {/snippet}
        </Item>
      {/each}
    </ItemGroup>
  {/if}
</Layout>
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Next, the page for one list. Look at `InfiniteScroll`. It wraps your rows and does the loading for you.

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
// ClientApp/pages/Lists/Show.tsx
import { InfiniteScroll, Link, router, useForm } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { ArrowLeft, BellRing, Copy, ListTodo, Plus, Trash2 } from 'lucide-react'
import type { FormEvent } from 'react'
import { Alert, AlertDescription } from '@/components/ui/alert'
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/checkbox'
import { Empty, EmptyDescription, EmptyHeader, EmptyMedia, EmptyTitle } from '@/components/ui/empty'
import { FieldError } from '@/components/ui/field'
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
import { Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemGroup, ItemMedia, ItemSeparator, ItemTitle } from '@/components/ui/item'
import { Label } from '@/components/ui/label'
import { Switch } from '@/components/ui/switch'
import Layout from '../../Layout'
import type { InertiaPages } from '../../types/inertia'
import { routes, type RouteBodies } from '../../types/routes'

export default function Show({ list, items }: InertiaPages['Lists/Show']) {
  const form = useForm<RouteBodies['items.store']>({ title: '', remindAt: null })

  const submit = (e: FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    form.submit(routes.items.store(list.id), { onSuccess: () => form.reset() })
  }

  return (
    <Layout>
      <div>
        <Button asChild variant="ghost" size="sm" className="-ml-2">
          <Link href={routes.lists.index()}><ArrowLeft /> All lists</Link>
        </Button>
        <div className="mt-1 flex items-center justify-between gap-4">
          <h1 className="text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight">{list.title}</h1>
          <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <Switch id="shared" checked={list.isShared} onCheckedChange={() => router.visit(routes.lists.share(list.id))} />
            <Label htmlFor="shared">Shared</Label>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      {list.shareUrl && (
        <Alert>
          <AlertDescription className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
            <span>Anyone with this link can read the list: <a className="underline" href={list.shareUrl}>{list.shareUrl}</a></span>
            <Button variant="outline" size="xs" onClick={() => navigator.clipboard.writeText(location.origin + list.shareUrl)}>
              <Copy /> Copy
            </Button>
          </AlertDescription>
        </Alert>
      )}

      <Card>
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Add an item</CardTitle>
          <CardDescription>Pick a time if you want a reminder.</CardDescription>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <form onSubmit={submit} className="space-y-2">
            <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
              <Input
                className="min-w-0 flex-1"
                value={form.data.title ?? ''}
                onChange={(e) => form.setData('title', e.target.value)}
                placeholder="What needs doing?"
                aria-invalid={Boolean(form.errors.title)}
              />
              <Input
                type="datetime-local"
                title="Remind me at"
                className="w-auto"
                onChange={(e) => form.setData('remindAt', e.target.value ? new Date(e.target.value).toISOString() : null)}
              />
              <Button disabled={form.processing}><Plus /> Add</Button>
            </div>
            <FieldError>{form.errors.title}</FieldError>
          </form>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>

      <Card className="py-0">
        <CardContent className="px-0">
          {/* InfiniteScroll loads the next page at the end of the list and merges it into items.data. The "?." is there
              because a prop made with Scroll() can be left out by a partial reload, so its generated type is optional. */}
          <InfiniteScroll data="items">
            {items?.data.length === 0 && (
              <Empty>
                <EmptyHeader>
                  <EmptyMedia variant="icon"><ListTodo /></EmptyMedia>
                  <EmptyTitle>Nothing here yet</EmptyTitle>
                  <EmptyDescription>Add the first item above.</EmptyDescription>
                </EmptyHeader>
              </Empty>
            )}
            <ItemGroup className="gap-0">
              {items?.data.map((item, i) => (
                <div key={item.id}>
                  {i > 0 && <ItemSeparator className="my-0" />}
                  <Item size="sm">
                    <ItemMedia>
                      <Checkbox
                        checked={item.isDone}
                        onCheckedChange={() => router.visit(routes.items.toggle(item.id), { preserveScroll: true })}
                        aria-label={`Mark ${item.title} as done`}
                      />
                    </ItemMedia>
                    <ItemContent>
                      <ItemTitle className={item.isDone ? 'text-muted-foreground line-through' : undefined}>
                        {item.title}
                        {item.remindAt && !item.isDone && <Badge variant="secondary"><BellRing /> reminder</Badge>}
                      </ItemTitle>
                    </ItemContent>
                    <ItemActions>
                      <Button
                        variant="ghost"
                        size="icon-sm"
                        aria-label={`Delete ${item.title}`}
                        onClick={() => router.visit(routes.items.destroy(item.id), { preserveScroll: true })}
                      >
                        <Trash2 />
                      </Button>
                    </ItemActions>
                  </Item>
                </div>
              ))}
            </ItemGroup>
          </InfiniteScroll>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </Layout>
  )
}
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue

<script setup lang="ts">
import { InfiniteScroll, Link, router, useForm } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
import { ArrowLeft, BellRing, Copy, ListTodo, Plus, Trash2 } from '@lucide/vue'
import { Alert, AlertDescription } from '@/components/ui/alert'
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/checkbox'
import { Empty, EmptyDescription, EmptyHeader, EmptyMedia, EmptyTitle } from '@/components/ui/empty'
import { FieldError } from '@/components/ui/field'
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
import { Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemGroup, ItemMedia, ItemSeparator, ItemTitle } from '@/components/ui/item'
import { Label } from '@/components/ui/label'

import Layout from '../../Layout.vue'
import type { InertiaPages } from '../../types/inertia'
import { routes, type RouteBodies } from '../../types/routes'

const props = defineProps<InertiaPages['Lists/Show']>()

const form = useForm<RouteBodies['items.store']>({ title: '', remindAt: null })
const submit = () => form.submit(routes.items.store(props.list.id), { onSuccess: () => form.reset() })
const setReminder = (e: Event) => {
  const value = (e.target as HTMLInputElement).value
  form.remindAt = value ? new Date(value).toISOString() : null
}
const copy = () => navigator.clipboard.writeText(location.origin + props.list.shareUrl)
</script>

<template>
  <Layout>
    <div>
      <Button as-child variant="ghost" size="sm" class="-ml-2">
        <Link :href="routes.lists.index()"><ArrowLeft /> All lists</Link>
      </Button>

        <h1 class="text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight">{{ list.title }}</h1>
        <div class="flex items-center gap-2">
          <Switch id="shared" :model-value="list.isShared" @update:model-value="router.visit(routes.lists.share(list.id))" />
          <Label for="shared">Shared</Label>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <Alert v-if="list.shareUrl">
      <AlertDescription class="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
        <span>Anyone with this link can read the list: <a class="underline" :href="list.shareUrl">{{ list.shareUrl }}</a></span>
        <Button variant="outline" size="xs" @click="copy"><Copy /> Copy</Button>
      </AlertDescription>
    </Alert>

    <Card>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Add an item</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>Pick a time if you want a reminder.</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <form class="space-y-2" @submit.prevent="submit">
          <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
            <Input :model-value="form.title ?? ''" @update:model-value="form.title = String($event)" class="min-w-0 flex-1" placeholder="What needs doing?" :aria-invalid="Boolean(form.errors.title)" />
            <Input type="datetime-local" title="Remind me at" class="w-auto" @change="setReminder" />
            <Button :disabled="form.processing"><Plus /> Add</Button>
          </div>
          <FieldError v-if="form.errors.title">{{ form.errors.title }}</FieldError>
        </form>
      </CardContent>
    </Card>

    <Card class="py-0">
      <CardContent class="px-0">
        <!-- InfiniteScroll loads the next page at the end of the list and merges it into items.data. The "?." is there
             because a prop made with Scroll() can be left out by a partial reload, so its generated type is optional. -->
        <InfiniteScroll data="items">
          <Empty v-if="items?.data.length === 0">
            <EmptyHeader>
              <EmptyMedia variant="icon"><ListTodo /></EmptyMedia>
              <EmptyTitle>Nothing here yet</EmptyTitle>
              <EmptyDescription>Add the first item above.</EmptyDescription>
            </EmptyHeader>

              <ItemSeparator v-if="i > 0" class="my-0" />

                <ItemMedia>
                  <Checkbox
                    :model-value="item.isDone"
                    :aria-label="`Mark ${item.title} as done`"
                    @update:model-value="router.visit(routes.items.toggle(item.id), { preserveScroll: true })"
                  />
                </ItemMedia>
                <ItemContent>
                  <ItemTitle :class="item.isDone ? 'text-muted-foreground line-through' : undefined">
                    {{ item.title }}
                    <Badge v-if="item.remindAt && !item.isDone" variant="secondary"><BellRing /> reminder</Badge>
                  </ItemTitle>
                </ItemContent>
                <ItemActions>
                  <Button
                    variant="ghost"
                    size="icon-sm"
                    :aria-label="`Delete ${item.title}`"
                    @click="router.visit(routes.items.destroy(item.id), { preserveScroll: true })"
                  >
                    <Trash2 />
                  </Button>
                </ItemActions>
              </Item>
            </div>
```

Try it:

1. Open **My lists** and click **Add** with the box empty. The server answers with "The Title field is required".
2. Paste a title longer than 80 characters and click outside the box. The error appears **before** you submit. That is Precognition. The message is the same one the server would send.
3. Add a list, add a few items, tick one off and add a reminder. The numbers at the top change, because every write cleared the cached stats.

<Callout type="info" title="Two small things you will notice">
- **`<Deferred>` needs a `fallback`**, even an empty one, or the page will not render. For the stats we show skeleton cards. For the reminders we show nothing until they arrive.
- **A change reloads the list from the first page.** When you tick an item, the server sends the list again, so the extra pages you loaded by scrolling are dropped. That is the cost of the simple `Back()` redirect. If it matters for your app, reload only what changed with a [partial reload](/docs/partial-reloads).
</Callout>

<Callout type="warning" title="Svelte: submit buttons need type=submit">
shadcn-svelte's `Button` is `type="button"` by default, so inside a form it does nothing. That is why the Svelte pages write `type="submit"` on their Add buttons. The React and Vue buttons submit by default.
</Callout>

## 7. Share a list, and render it on the server

A shared list is a page that anyone can open, and many people may open the same one. That makes it a good page for **server-side rendering (SSR)**.

Without SSR, the server sends an empty page. The browser has to download JavaScript, run it, and only then show the list. With SSR, the server runs your component first and sends finished HTML. Search engines and slow phones get the content at once. The browser then makes the page interactive with the same code.

The share button already exists, from step 6. Only the page it points to is missing.

Create `PublicPage.cs`, add `[JsonSerializable(typeof(PublicPage))]` to `AppJsonContext`, and map the route. The route goes in `Endpoints.cs`:

```csharp
// inside MapForgetMeNot, at the end. No sign-in here: anyone with the link can read the list.
app.MapGet("/p/{slug}", PublicPage.Handle).WithName("public.show");
```

This is the page record, in `PublicPage.cs`:

```csharp
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

namespace ForgetMeNot;

public sealed record PublicPage(
    PublicHeader List,
    [property: InertiaPropType(typeof(Page<PublicItem>))] InertiaProp Items) : IInertiaPage
{
    public static string Component => "Public/Show";

    public static async Task<IResult> Handle(
        string slug, PageRequest request, AppDb db, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var list = await db.Lists.AsNoTracking()
            .Where(l => l.ShareSlug == slug)
            .Select(l => new PublicHeader(l.Title, l.Items.Count(i => !i.IsDone)))
            .FirstOrDefaultAsync(ct);
        if (list is null) return Results.NotFound();

        var items = await db.Items.AsNoTracking()
            .Where(i => i.List.ShareSlug == slug && !i.IsDone)
            .OrderBy(i => i.Id)
            .Select(i => new PublicItem(i.Id, i.Title))
            .ToPageAsync(request, ct: ct);

        // Everyone sees the same page, so the server-rendered HTML can be reused: fresh for 5 minutes, then
        // served for up to an
        // hour more while a new render is made in the background. The cache key includes the page's JSON,
        // so a changed list is
        // never served from an old render.
        return Render(new PublicPage(list, Scroll(items))).WithSsrCache(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5), staleFor: TimeSpan.FromHours(1));
    }
}
```

Look at the last line. `.WithSsrCache(...)` is the **SSR cache**. Rendering takes time, and this page looks the same for everyone, so the app can reuse the finished HTML:

- For **5 minutes**, the app serves the saved HTML without calling the SSR server at all.
- For **one hour more**, the app still serves the saved HTML and makes a new render in the background (`staleFor`). Nobody waits.
- The cache key is built from the page's **JSON**, which includes the title and the items. If the list changes, the JSON changes, the key changes, and the old render is never used. You cannot show a stale page by mistake.

<Callout type="warning" title="Cache only pages that everyone sees the same">
A page with per-person props makes one cache entry per person. That wastes memory and gains nothing. The list pages in this app are **not** cached for that reason. The public page is cached.
</Callout>

Turn SSR on. In `AddInertia(...)` in `Program.cs`, add:

```csharp
// Server-side rendering: Bun runs the bundle that "vite build --ssr" writes. While Vite runs in
// development, Vite renders instead.
o.Ssr.BundlePath = "ssr/ssr.js";
o.Ssr.UseNodeProcess(n => n.Executable = "bun");
```

`UseNodeProcess` makes the app start and watch the SSR process for you. If the SSR process stops answering, the app restarts it. While the SSR process is down, the pages are rendered in the browser instead. Use `n.Executable = "node"` if you do not have Bun.

<Callout type="warning" title="Two apps on one machine">
The SSR process listens on port 13714. If a second Inertia.Net app on the same machine tries to start its own SSR process, that process cannot start. The second app then renders in the browser instead, without an error. You see a warning in the log. To avoid this, give each app its own port:

1. Set the port in C#: `o.Ssr.UseNodeProcess(n => { n.Executable = "bun"; n.BasePort = 13715; })`.
2. Set the same port in the `inertia({ ssr: { port: ... } })` line of `vite.config.ts`.
3. Run the build again.

The port is written into the SSR bundle when the bundle is built, so changing only the C# side does not work. We ran two apps side by side this way and both rendered on the server.
</Callout>

The SSR bundle needs an entry file and a build setting. The entry file has two lines:

```tsx
// ClientApp/ssr.tsx (ClientApp/ssr.ts for Vue and Svelte, importing from @inertiajs/vue3 or @inertiajs/svelte)
import { createInertiaApp } from '@inertiajs/react'

createInertiaApp()
```

In `vite.config.ts`, tell the Inertia plugin where the entry file is. Also build the SSR bundle into the `ssr` folder with its dependencies included, so the bundle runs without `node_modules`:

```ts
export default defineConfig(({ command, isSsrBuild }) => ({
  plugins: [react(), tailwindcss(), inertia({ ssr: { entry: 'ClientApp/ssr.tsx', host: '127.0.0.1', port: 13714 } }), hotFile()],
  ssr: isSsrBuild ? { noExternal: true } : undefined,
  build: isSsrBuild
    ? { outDir: 'ssr', emptyOutDir: true }
    : { outDir: 'wwwroot/build', emptyOutDir: true, manifest: true, rolldownOptions: { input: 'ClientApp/app.tsx' } },
  // ...the rest stays the same. For Vue and Svelte, the entries are ssr.ts and app.ts.
}))
```

Change the `build` script in `package.json` so it builds both bundles:

```json
{ "scripts": { "build": "tsc --noEmit && vite build && vite build --ssr" } }
```

Instead of `tsc --noEmit`, use `vue-tsc --noEmit` for Vue or `svelte-check --tsgo --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json` for Svelte. The template's script already has the right command. Only add the last part.

Then add the public page:

<Tabs>
  <Tab label="React">

```tsx
// ClientApp/pages/Public/Show.tsx
import { InfiniteScroll } from '@inertiajs/react'
import { Circle } from 'lucide-react'
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
import { Card, CardContent } from '@/components/ui/card'
import { Item, ItemContent, ItemGroup, ItemMedia, ItemSeparator, ItemTitle } from '@/components/ui/item'
import Layout from '../../Layout'
import type { InertiaPages } from '../../types/inertia'

export default function Show({ list, items }: InertiaPages['Public/Show']) {
  return (
    <Layout>
      <div>
        <Badge variant="secondary">Shared list</Badge>
        <h1 className="mt-3 text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight">{list.title}</h1>
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{list.open} open items</p>
      </div>
      <Card className="py-0">
        <CardContent className="px-0">
          <InfiniteScroll data="items">
            <ItemGroup className="gap-0">
              {items?.data.map((item, i) => (
                <div key={item.id}>
                  {i > 0 && <ItemSeparator className="my-0" />}
                  <Item size="sm">
                    <ItemMedia><Circle className="size-4 text-muted-foreground" /></ItemMedia>
                    <ItemContent><ItemTitle>{item.title}</ItemTitle></ItemContent>
                  </Item>
                </div>
              ))}
            </ItemGroup>
          </InfiniteScroll>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </Layout>
  )
}
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Vue">

```vue

  import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
  import { Card, CardContent } from '@/components/ui/card'
```

```svelte
<Layout>
  <div>
    <Badge variant="secondary">Shared list</Badge>
    <h1 class="mt-3 text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight">{list.title}</h1>
```

  </Tab>

<Callout type="info" title="Your component runs on the server too">
During SSR, the code in a page runs in Node or Bun, where there is no `window` or `document`. That is why `Show` uses a relative link and not `window.location.origin`. If a component must use the browser, do that inside an effect, which runs only in the browser.
</Callout>

To see SSR work, build the app, start it in the Production setting, and look at the page source of a shared list. The list title and the items are there as real HTML:

```sh
bun run build
ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production dotnet run
```

While Vite runs in development, Vite does the rendering itself and the SSR cache is switched off, so every change shows at once. That is why you build and run in Production to see the real behavior.

## 8. A reminder that appears by itself

You can add a reminder time to an item. When the time comes, the **My lists** page should show the reminder, without anyone reloading. Two parts make that work: a **worker** that notices due reminders, and a **live prop** that refreshes the page when it is told to.

Start with the worker. A `BackgroundService` runs for as long as the app runs:

```csharp
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

namespace ForgetMeNot;

// / <summary>Every 20 seconds: find reminders that are due, mark them as sent, and tell the owner's open
// pages to refresh.</summary>
public sealed class ReminderWorker(IServiceScopeFactory scopes, ILogger<ReminderWorker> logger) : BackgroundService
{
    protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken)
    {
        using var timer = new PeriodicTimer(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(20));
        while (await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken))
        {
            try
            {
                await SendDueRemindersAsync(stoppingToken);
            }
            catch (Exception e) when (e is not OperationCanceledException)
            {
                logger.LogError(e, "Sending reminders failed; trying again on the next tick");
            }
        }
    }

    private async Task SendDueRemindersAsync(CancellationToken ct)
    {
        using var scope = scopes.CreateScope(); // the worker lives forever, but a DbContext should not
        var db = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<AppDb>();
        var live = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IInertiaLive>();
        var now = DateTime.UtcNow;

        var due = await db.Items.Include(i => i.List)
            .Where(i => i.RemindAt != null && i.RemindAt <= now && i.RemindedAt == null)
            .Take(100)
            .ToListAsync(ct);

        // saved before publishing, so a restart cannot send it twice
        foreach (var item in due) item.RemindedAt = now;
        await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);

        foreach (var email in due.Select(i => i.List.OwnerEmail).Distinct())
        {
            await live.PublishAsync(Events.RemindersChanged(email), cancellationToken: ct);
        }

        if (due.Count > 0) logger.LogInformation("Sent {Count} reminders", due.Count);
    }
}
```

- **Every 20 seconds** is enough for a demo. A real app might use a minute.
- **`CreateScope()`** gives the worker its own `AppDb`. The worker runs for as long as the app runs, but a database context must not live that long.
- **Save first, publish second.** The worker marks the reminders as sent before it tells anyone. If the app stops between the two steps, nobody gets the same reminder twice.
- **`try`/`catch` around the work.** If one round fails, the worker logs the error and tries again next time. It does not stop.

Now look at the line that connects the worker to the page. In `ListsPage`, you wrote `.Live(Events.RemindersChanged(email))`. When the worker publishes that event, the browser reloads **only** the `reminders` prop. Nothing else on the page changes.

Install the SignalR transport. It carries the "something changed" message to the browser:

```sh
dotnet add package Inertia.Net.Live.SignalR --version 1.9.8
bun add @microsoft/signalr
```

In `Program.cs`, register the SignalR transport and the worker, and map the connection endpoint:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddHostedService<ReminderWorker>();

// Live props: the server can tell a signed-in browser that something changed.
builder.Services.AddInertiaLive().AddSignalR(o =>
    o.Authorize((context, channel, ct) =>
        ValueTask.FromResult(channel.Name == $"users.{context.User?.FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.Email)}")));

// ...after app.MapInertiaDevTools();
app.MapInertiaLiveHub(); // the SignalR connection, at /inertia-live
```

<Callout type="danger" title="This Authorize rule is the security">
Without it, nobody can join a private channel. With it, a person can join only the channel named after their own email. Without this check, anyone could listen to anyone's reminders. Keep the rule tight.
</Callout>

Finally, turn the client side on. The template already includes `ClientApp/lib/inertia-signalr.ts`. Import it in the client entry (`app.tsx` or `app.ts`) and pass it to `createInertiaApp`:

```ts
import { signalr } from './lib/inertia-signalr'

createInertiaApp({
  serverHead: true,
  live: signalr(), // props marked .Live(...) refresh themselves when the server publishes their event
})
```

Run the app. Add an item with a reminder one minute from now, open **My lists** and wait. When the time comes, the reminder appears without a reload. Open the browser's network tab to see how little happens: one small request, only for `reminders`.

<Callout type="info" title="Why not just poll?">
Polling asks "anything new?" every few seconds, for every open page, all day. A live prop sends nothing until something changes, and then sends one small request. A live prop is cheaper for the server and faster for the person.
</Callout>

<Callout type="warning" title="More than one server">
A SignalR message reaches only the browsers connected to the server that sent it. Each server would also run its own worker. Behind a load balancer, do these things:

- Add a Redis backplane.
- Keep the props cache in Redis (see [Redis cache](/docs/redis)).
- Run the worker on one instance.

For a single server, the setup you have now is correct.
</Callout>

## 9. Test the important paths

The app has a few rules it must never break:

- Nobody reads another person's list.
- A private list has no public page.
- The dashboard's slow numbers arrive after the page.

Tests make sure these rules stay true.

Create a test project next to the app. Make sure its `TargetFramework` matches the app's:

```sh
dotnet new xunit -n ForgetMeNot.Tests
cd ForgetMeNot.Tests
dotnet add reference ../ForgetMeNot/ForgetMeNot.csproj
dotnet add package Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing --version "10.*"
dotnet add package Inertia.Net.Testing --version 1.9.8
```

The test project starts your real app in memory. For that to work, add one line at the very end of the app's `Program.cs`:

```csharp
public partial class Program; // lets the test project start the app
```

Delete the generated `UnitTest1.cs` and create `ListTests.cs`:

```csharp
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Json;
using Inertia.Net;
using Inertia.Net.Testing;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;

namespace ForgetMeNot.Tests;

public sealed class ListTests : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>, IDisposable
{
    private readonly string _db = Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), $"forgetmenot-{Guid.NewGuid():N}.db");
    private readonly HttpClient _client;

    public ListTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory)
    {
        // A fresh SQLite file per test class, a fixed asset version, and no SSR server to start.
        _client = factory.WithWebHostBuilder(builder =>
        {
            builder.UseSetting("ConnectionStrings:Default", $"Data Source={_db}");
            builder.ConfigureTestServices(services => services.PostConfigure<InertiaOptions>(o =>
            {
                o.Version = "test";
                o.Ssr.Mode = SsrMode.Disabled;
            }));
        }).CreateClient(new WebApplicationFactoryClientOptions { AllowAutoRedirect = false, HandleCookies = true });
    }

    public void Dispose()
    {
        _client.Dispose();
        foreach (var file in Directory.GetFiles(Path.GetTempPath(), Path.GetFileName(_db) + "*")) File.Delete(file);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Lists_need_a_signed_in_person()
    {
        using var response = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/lists", version: "test");

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Redirect, response.StatusCode);
        Assert.Contains("/login", response.Headers.Location!.ToString());
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task A_list_can_be_created_filled_and_shared()
    {
        await SignInAsync();

        // Create a list. The POST redirects to the new list's page.
        using var created = await PostAsync("/lists", new { title = "Groceries" }, referer: "/lists");
        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Redirect, created.StatusCode);
        Assert.Equal("/lists/1", created.Headers.Location!.ToString());

        // Add an item, then look at the list. Items are a scroll prop: a "Page" of rows.
        using var added = await PostAsync("/lists/1/items", new { title = "Milk" }, referer: "/lists/1");
        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Redirect, added.StatusCode); // Back() sends the person to the page they came from

        using var show = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/lists/1", version: "test");
        await show.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page
            .Component("Lists/Show")
            .Has("list", list => list.Where("title", "Groceries").Where("isShared", false).Etc())
            .HasScroll("items")
            .Has("items.data", 1, first => first.Where("title", "Milk").Etc()));

        // Nobody can read a private list from the public address.
        using var notYet = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/p/not-a-real-link", version: "test");
        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.NotFound, notYet.StatusCode);

        // Share it, then read the public page.
        using var shared = await PostAsync("/lists/1/share", new { }, referer: "/lists/1");
        using var afterShare = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/lists/1", version: "test");
        var shareUrl = (await afterShare.GetInertiaPageAsync()).Prop("list.shareUrl")!.ToString()!; // "/p/<secret>"

        using var publicPage = await _client.InertiaGetAsync(shareUrl, version: "test");
        await publicPage.AssertInertiaAsync(page => page
            .Component("Public/Show")
            .Has("list", list => list.Where("title", "Groceries").Where("open", 1).Etc())
            .Has("items.data", 1, first => first.Where("title", "Milk").Missing("remindAt").Etc()));
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task The_dashboard_defers_its_slow_props_and_listens_for_reminders()
    {
        await SignInAsync();
        using var created = await PostAsync("/lists", new { title = "Work" }, referer: "/lists");
        using var added = await PostAsync("/lists/1/items", new { title = "Write tests" }, referer: "/lists/1");

        var page = await (await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/lists", version: "test")).GetInertiaPageAsync();
        new AssertableInertia(page)
            .Component("Lists/Index")
            .HasDeferred("stats")
            .Missing("stats")
            .HasLive("reminders", "private:users.demo@example.com", "RemindersChanged");

        var loaded = await page.LoadDeferredPropsAsync(_client);
        new AssertableInertia(loaded).Has("stats", stats => stats.Where("open", 1).Where("done", 0).Etc());
    }


    private async Task SignInAsync()
    {
        using var form = await _client.InertiaGetAsync("/login", version: "test");
        using var request = JsonRequest(HttpMethod.Post, "/login", new { email = "demo@example.com", password = "password" }, "/login");
        request.WithXsrfToken(form);
        using var response = await _client.SendAsync(request);
        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Redirect, response.StatusCode);
    }

    private async Task<HttpResponseMessage> PostAsync(string url, object body, string referer)
    {
        // The XSRF cookie is issued on any page response; read the token from one and send it back as a header.
        using var any = await _client.InertiaGetAsync(referer, version: "test");
        using var request = JsonRequest(HttpMethod.Post, url, body, referer);
        request.WithXsrfToken(any);
        return await _client.SendAsync(request);
    }

    private HttpRequestMessage JsonRequest(HttpMethod method, string url, object body, string referer)
    {
        var request = new HttpRequestMessage(method, url) { Content = JsonContent.Create(body) };
        request.Headers.Add("X-Inertia", "true");
        request.Headers.Add("X-Inertia-Version", "test");
        request.Headers.Add("X-Requested-With", "XMLHttpRequest");
        request.Headers.Referrer = new Uri(_client.BaseAddress!, referer);
        return request;
    }
}
```

Read the setup, because it explains most of the rest:

- **A fresh database file per test class.** Tests must not see each other's lists.
- **`o.Version = "test"`** fixes the asset version, so requests do not need a first visit to learn it.
- **`SsrMode.Disabled`** means the tests do not start Bun.
- **`AllowAutoRedirect = false`** lets a test look at the redirect itself, such as "a signed-out visitor is sent to `/login`".
- **`HandleCookies = true`** keeps the sign-in cookie and the anti-forgery cookie between requests, like a browser.

Run the tests:

```sh
dotnet test
```

<Callout type="info" title="Why does the helper read an XSRF token?">
The template protects every form against cross-site request forgery (CSRF). A real browser gets a cookie and sends it back as a header. In a test, `WithXsrfToken` copies the token from a page response into your request, so the server accepts the request. If a test fails with a 400, a missing token is usually the reason.
</Callout>

## 10. Run it in production

Build both bundles and publish:

```sh
bun run build
dotnet publish -c Release
```

Before the app is public, go through this short list. Each item has a reason.

| Do this | Why |
|---|---|
| Install Bun (or set `Executable = "node"`) where the app runs | The app starts the SSR bundle with it |
| Keep the Data Protection keys somewhere that survives a restart | The sign-in cookie is encrypted with them. A new key signs everyone out |
| Use EF Core migrations instead of `EnsureCreated()` | The tables will change, and `EnsureCreated()` cannot change them |
| Set `ConnectionStrings__Default` for the real database | The file next to the app is only for your laptop |
| Forward the proxy headers when you run behind one | The sign-in rate limit counts clients by address. Without the headers, every client looks like the proxy. See [Deploying behind a proxy](/docs/deploying) |
| Run one instance, or add Redis for the caches and SignalR | The props cache, SSR cache and live messages are per server unless you share them |

Container examples are in [Deploying behind a proxy](/docs/deploying) and the [server-side rendering](/docs/server-side-rendering) guide. For the container's memory, use the [memory table](/docs/performance#memory-and-hosting).

## If something does not build

Compare your `Program.cs` with the finished one:

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem title="The finished Program.cs">

```csharp
using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
using System.Security.Claims;
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;
using System.Threading.RateLimiting;
using ForgetMeNot;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Cookies;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Props are serialized through the app's source-generated JSON context.
builder.Services.ConfigureHttpJsonOptions(o => o.SerializerOptions.TypeInfoResolverChain.Insert(0, AppJsonContext.Default));
builder.Services.AddValidation();
// CSRF: the Inertia client sends the XSRF-TOKEN cookie back as X-XSRF-TOKEN; UseInertiaAntiforgery() issues and validates it.
builder.Services.AddAntiforgery(o => o.HeaderName = InertiaHeaders.XsrfToken);
builder.Services.AddResponseCompression();
builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDb>(o =>
    o.UseSqlite(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Default") ?? "Data Source=forgetmenot.db"));
builder.Services.AddHostedService<ReminderWorker>();
builder.Services.AddSingleton<UserStore>();
// Cookie sign-in. UseInertiaRedirects(): an Inertia visit to a protected page is redirected to /login like a browser request
// (303 after a POST, PUT or DELETE), not answered with 401.
builder.Services.AddAuthentication(CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
    .AddCookie(o =>
    {
        o.LoginPath = "/login";
        o.UseInertiaRedirects();
    });
builder.Services.AddAuthorization();
// At most 5 sign-in attempts a minute per client. Precognition requests (checking a field as you type) get their own allowance of 30 a
// minute, so typing doesn't use up sign-in attempts and validation can't be called without limit.
// Behind a reverse proxy every client has the proxy's address: configure forwarded headers first (README, "Deploying behind a proxy").
builder.Services.AddRateLimiter(o =>
{
    o.AddPolicy("login", http =>
    {
        var client = http.Connection.RemoteIpAddress?.ToString() ?? "unknown";
        // The metadata check keeps the Precognition header from skipping the limit on an endpoint whose handler runs for it.
        return http.GetEndpoint()?.Metadata.GetMetadata<InertiaPrecognitionMetadata>() is not null && InertiaPrecognition.IsPrecognitive(http.Request)
            ? RateLimitPartition.GetSlidingWindowLimiter("validation:" + client,
                _ => new SlidingWindowRateLimiterOptions { PermitLimit = 30, Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1), SegmentsPerWindow = 6 })
            : RateLimitPartition.GetFixedWindowLimiter("login:" + client,
                _ => new FixedWindowRateLimiterOptions { PermitLimit = 5, Window = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1) });
    });
    o.OnRejected = InertiaRateLimiting.OnRejected(); // back to the form, with flash.error
});
// Live props: the server can push "something changed" to a signed-in browser. A person may only join their own channel.
builder.Services.AddInertiaLive().AddSignalR(o =>
    o.Authorize((context, channel, ct) =>
        ValueTask.FromResult(channel.Name == $"users.{context.User?.FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.Email)}")));
builder.Services.AddInertia(o =>
{
    o.Share("appName", "ForgetMeNot");
    // The signed-in user on every page (page.props.auth.user), typed in the generated SharedProps.
    o.Share("auth", http => new Auth(http.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true
        ? new AuthUser(http.User.FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.Name)!, http.User.FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.Email)!)
        : null));
    o.Vite.Prefetch = VitePrefetch.Waterfall; // fetch the other pages' chunks once a page has loaded
    // Development only: rendering a component without a page file fails fast, and ClientApp/types/inertia.d.ts (from these
    // C# types) and ClientApp/types/routes.ts (from the named endpoints below) are rewritten when the app starts.
    o.Pages.Directory = "ClientApp/pages";
    o.TypeScript.OutputPath = "ClientApp/types/inertia.d.ts";
    o.TypeScript.RoutesOutputPath = "ClientApp/types/routes.ts";
    o.TypeScript.AddGeneratedPages().FlashData<Flash>(); // every IInertiaPage record, listed at compile time
    // Server-side rendering: Bun runs the bundle that "vite build --ssr" writes. While Vite runs in development, Vite renders instead.
    o.Ssr.BundlePath = "ssr/ssr.js";
    o.Ssr.UseNodeProcess(n => n.Executable = "bun");
});
// Render the Error page for production navigation errors; Development keeps its diagnostics.
builder.Services.AddInertiaErrorPages();
builder.Services.AddInertiaDevTools(); // the Inertia DevTools browser extension, in Development only

var app = builder.Build();

using (var scope = app.Services.CreateScope())
{
    scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<AppDb>().Database.EnsureCreated(); // fine for a first app; use migrations later
}

app.UseResponseCompression();
app.UseStaticFiles(new StaticFileOptions
{
    // Vite puts a content hash in every file name under build/assets, so browsers can keep them for good.
    OnPrepareResponse = c =>
    {
        if (c.Context.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments("/build/assets"))
        {
            c.Context.Response.Headers.CacheControl = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
        }
    },
});
app.UseInertiaErrorPages(); // before UseInertia(): also handles unmatched routes and unhandled exceptions
app.UseInertia();
app.UseAuthentication(); // after UseInertiaErrorPages(): a 403 renders the Error page
app.UseAuthorization();
app.UseRateLimiter(); // after UseInertia(): a rejected sign-in redirects back with a flash message
app.UseInertiaAntiforgery(); // after UseAuthentication(): the token is tied to the signed-in user
app.MapInertiaDevTools();
app.MapInertiaLiveHub(); // the SignalR hub at /inertia-live

app.MapInertia("/", HomePage.Component, new HomePage("Welcome to ForgetMeNot, an Inertia.js app on ASP.NET Core.")).WithName("home");

// The cookie handler sends signed-out visitors here with ?ReturnUrl=/the/page; the form posts it back.
app.MapGet("/login", (string? returnUrl) => Render(new LoginPage(returnUrl))).WithName("login");

// WithInertiaPrecognition(): the form checks each field as you leave it, with the same validation as the submit.
app.MapPost("/login", async (HttpContext http, UserStore users, LoginInput input) =>
{
    if (users.Find(input.Email!, input.Password!) is not { } user)
    {
        return Back("/login").WithErrors(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["email"] = "These credentials do not match our records." });
    }

    var identity = new ClaimsIdentity(
        [new Claim(ClaimTypes.Name, user.Name), new Claim(ClaimTypes.Email, user.Email)], CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme);
    await http.SignInAsync(new ClaimsPrincipal(identity));

    // Only a path on this site: an absolute or protocol-relative URL here would be an open redirect.
    return Results.Redirect(input.ReturnUrl is ['/'] or ['/', not ('/' or '\\'), ..] ? input.ReturnUrl : "/lists");
}).WithInertiaPrecognition().RequireRateLimiting("login").WithName("login.store");

app.MapPost("/logout", async (HttpContext http) =>
{
    await http.SignOutAsync();
    return Results.Redirect("/");
}).WithName("logout");

app.MapForgetMeNot(); // our lists, items and the public page

app.Run();

public partial class Program; // lets the test project start the app

namespace ForgetMeNot
{
    // A page record names its client component once: Render(new HomePage(...)) and o.TypeScript.Page<HomePage>() both use it.
    public sealed record HomePage(string Message) : IInertiaPage
    {
        public static string Component => "Home";
    }

    /// <summary>The flash data the pages read (<c>page.flash</c>).</summary>
    public sealed record Flash(string? Success, string? Error);

    public sealed record LoginPage(string? ReturnUrl) : IInertiaPage
    {
        public static string Component => "Auth/Login";
    }

    /// <summary>The shared <c>auth</c> prop: the signed-in user, or null.</summary>
    public sealed record Auth(AuthUser? User);

    public sealed record AuthUser(string Name, string Email);

    public sealed class LoginInput
    {
        [Required, EmailAddress]
        public string? Email { get; set; }

        [Required]
        public string? Password { get; set; }

        /// <summary>Where to go after signing in: the page that sent the visitor to the login page.</summary>
        public string? ReturnUrl { get; set; }
    }

    /// <summary>One demo user (demo@example.com / password). Swap it for ASP.NET Core Identity or your user database.</summary>
    public sealed class UserStore
    {
        private readonly PasswordHasher<AuthUser> _hasher = new();
        private readonly AuthUser _demo = new("Demo User", "demo@example.com");
        private readonly string _hash;

        public UserStore() => _hash = _hasher.HashPassword(_demo, "password");

        public AuthUser? Find(string email, string password) =>
            string.Equals(email, _demo.Email, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            && _hasher.VerifyHashedPassword(_demo, _hash, password) != PasswordVerificationResult.Failed
                ? _demo
                : null;
    }

    [JsonSourceGenerationOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web)]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(HomePage))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(Flash))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(LoginPage))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(Auth))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(LoginInput))]
    // Our pages, props and forms. The template turns reflection-based JSON off, so each type is listed here.
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(ListsPage))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(ListPage))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(PublicPage))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(ListCard))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(Stats))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(List<ReminderRow>))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(Page<ItemRow>))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(Page<PublicItem>))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(NewList))]
    [JsonSerializable(typeof(NewItem))]
    internal sealed partial class AppJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext;
}
```

  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

## Where to go next

You used page records, named and typed routes, Precognition, deferred and cached props, `ToPageAsync`, infinite scroll, server-side rendering with its cache, live props and the testing helpers. These are the next ones to try:

- [Once props](/docs/once-props): remember a value that never changes on the client, such as a list of countries.
- [Merging props](/docs/merging-props) and [Partial reloads](/docs/partial-reloads): update part of a page without replacing it.
- [Redis cache](/docs/redis): share the props and SSR caches between servers.
- [Authentication](/docs/authentication): replace the demo user with ASP.NET Core Identity.
- [Native AOT](/docs/native-aot): a much smaller and faster-starting app, once you avoid EF Core.
- [Performance](/docs/performance): what each feature costs, measured.
